children.translated_text: Those by whose glorious name <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) [is obtained],
by whom all that is desired becomes [the attainment] of fortune —
having bowed to those worthy ones, I compose
a <s>vārttika</s> (commentary) on the <s>Kaṅkāla</s>-chapter.
Having heard something from the teachers,
having associated with some experts,
and having experienced something [myself] —
this text is expounded by me.
Even when taught directly by the <s>guru</s>,
the science of metals (<s>dhātuvāda</s>) does not succeed
until the practical procedure is witnessed
two or three times in the presence of the <s>guru</s>.
Therefore, even having heard [the teachings],
and having looked here and there,
those who make expenditures on materials [without guidance]
toil in vain, [being] foolish.
If, having become pleased, the true <s>guru</s>
demonstrates the entire procedure,
then even effortlessly, all
the preparations succeed without doubt.
Therefore, even though the meaning of the text
is clearly stated herein, on the principal authority,
one should not exert oneself in <s>dhātuvāda</s>
while disregarding the <s>gurus</s>.
He who speaks does not know;
he who knows does not speak.
Therefore, in this matter or that,
the wise should not open their mouths.
Skilled in mercury pills (<s>rasaguṭī</s>) and collyriums (<s>añjana</s>),
the <s>yogin</s> Śrī <s>Kaṅkālaya</s> was [the source];
by him, for the instruction of his own disciples,
the truth of mercury (<s>rasatattva</s>) was expounded.
And the disciple of Śrī <s>Kaṅkālaya</s> the <s>yogin</s>,
the skillful one, for the benefit of others,
composed the <s>Rasādhyāya</s>
in twenty-one chapters.

body.text: tatrādāv eva nirvighnaṃ prārabdhakāryasiddhyartham abhīṣṭadevatānamaskāram āha || 1
body.translated_text: Therein, at the very outset, for the accomplishment of the undertaken task without obstacles, he states the salutation to the chosen deity: ||1

children.translated_text: Having first bowed to Śrī <s>Bhairava</s>,
the omniscient lord of the three worlds,
and to Śrī <s>Bhāratī</s> and <s>Vighneśa</s> (Gaṇeśa),
I pay homage for the pacification of obstacles.
Celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>) and austerity (<s>tapas</s>) must be practiced,
[and] the eating of sacrificial food (<s>haviṣyānna</s>).
When the procedure is violated, [preparations] do not succeed;
when austerity is lost, they do not bear fruit.

body.text: iha rasakarmāṇi caturaśītiḥ guṭikābhedāścaturaśītiḥ añjanāni caturaśītiḥ || 1
body.translated_text: Herein, the mercury procedures [number] eighty-four; the pill varieties [number] eighty-four; the collyria [number] eighty-four. ||1

body.text: evaṃ te dvipañcāśadadhike dve śate bhedāḥ || 2
body.translated_text: Thus the [total] varieties are two hundred and fifty-two. ||2

body.text: tata eteṣāṃ bhedānāṃ madhyād yadaikā kācit kriyā prārabhyate tadā prārambhātpūrvaṃ māsamekaṃ brahmacaryarūpaṃ tapaḥ kartavyam || 3
body.translated_text: Then, from among these varieties, when any single procedure is undertaken, before the commencement, celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in the form of austerity must be practiced for one month. ||3
Because <s>brahmacarya</s> is the root of all austerities. ||4
Because all other austerity without it is fruitless. ||5
Alternatively, <s>brahmacarya</s> is to be maintained. ||6
And austerity is to be performed as appropriate through [the instruction of] the <s>ācārya</s> and others. ||7
Because both [brahmacarya and tapas] are the primary root of the fruits of all procedures. ||8

body.text: tathā haviṣyānnaṃ ghṛtaśarkarāmiśraṃ pāyasaṃ kṣīrabhojanaṃ kāryam || 9
body.translated_text: Likewise, <s>haviṣyānna</s> — payasam (milk-rice) mixed with ghee and sugar, and a diet of milk — is to be maintained. ||9
Because purity of the body is not achieved through other foods. ||10
And because the means of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> [practice] is absent [without it]. ||11

body.text: tata evaṃ karma pālayatā tatkarmaphalaṃ yāvan netavyam || 12
body.translated_text: Therefore, by one who maintains the procedure in this way, the fruit of that procedure is to be obtained. ||12

body.text: yato rasādikā kriyāḥ sādhake bhraṣṭe yathoktabhojanam akurvati na sidhyanti || 13
body.translated_text: Because mercury procedures and the like do not succeed for a practitioner who has deviated — who does not maintain the prescribed diet. ||13
And when austerity is lost, they do not bear fruit. ||14
And this he himself will clarify at the end of the text. ||15

children.translated_text: Now, the chapter that has been received
from the <s>yogin</s> Śrī <s>Kaṅkālaya</s> —
I shall expound [it], in which
the chain-mercury (<s>śṛṅkhalārasa</s>) is revealed through methods.

body.translated_text: 'I shall expound the chapter that has been received from the <s>yogin</s> Śrī <s>Kaṅkālaya</s>' — this is the disciple's statement. ||1
In which chapter the chain-mercury is made manifest through methods — processing with herbs, sublimation, firing in crucibles, and so forth. ||2

body.text: yathā kila śṛṅkhalā pūrvapūrvatarāvayavair anyonyānupraveśāt sambaddhā bhavati tathā atrāpi || 3
body.translated_text: Just as a chain (<s>śṛṅkhalā</s>) is connected by the mutual interlinking of successive links, so too here: ||3
First is the purification (<s>śodhana</s>) of mercury. ||4
Then the revival (<s>utthāpana</s>) of the stupefied (<s>mūrchita</s>) purified mercury. ||5
Then the precipitation (<s>pātana</s>) of the revived mercury. ||6
Then the re-revival of the precipitated [mercury]. ||7
Then the steaming (<s>svedana</s>) of the precipitated-and-revived [mercury]. ||8
Then the regulation (<s>niyāmana</s>) of the steamed [mercury]. ||9
Then the confinement (<s>nirodhana</s>) of the regulated [mercury]. ||10
Then the spreading-and-extending (<s>vakraprasāraṇa</s>) of the confined [mercury]. ||11
Then the digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>) of mica (<s>abhraka</s>) by the spread-and-extended [mercury]. ||12
Then the digestion of metals (<s>loha</s>) by [mercury] that has digested mica. ||13
Then the digestion of pyrite (<s>ayaḥprakāśarāji</s>) by [mercury] that has digested metals. ||14
Then the digestion of gold-line (<s>hemarāji</s>) by [mercury] that has digested pyrite. ||15
Then the digestion of sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>) by [mercury] that has digested gold-line. ||16
Then the digestion of the essence of realgar (<s>manaḥśilāsattva</s>) by [mercury] that has digested sulphur. ||17
Then the digestion of the essence of tin (<s>khāparasattva</s>) by [mercury] that has digested the essence of realgar. ||18
Then the digestion of diamond (<s>hīraka</s>) by [mercury] that has digested the essence of tin. ||19
Then the fixation (<s>bandha</s>) of [mercury] that has digested diamond. ||20
Then the liquefaction (<s>sāraṇa</s>) of the fixed [mercury]. ||21
Then the killing (<s>māraṇa</s>) of the liquefied [mercury]. ||22
Then the transmutation (<s>krāmaṇa</s>) of the killed [mercury]. ||23
Then the [final] fixation of the transmuted [mercury]. ||24
Then the unsealing (<s>udghāṭana</s>) of the fixed [mercury]. ||25
Thus. ||26

body.text: evaṃ pūrvapūrvatarasaṃskārasya rasasyāgretanasaṃskāro granthito'stīty asau procyata iti tattvam || 27
body.translated_text: In this way, the successive processing of mercury — each prior process leading to the next — is bound together in the text; thus it is called [chain-mercury]. ||27

children.translated_text: The defects of mercury (<s>sūta</s>), then the purification,
the processes (<s>saṃskāras</s>) — before [these] I shall state:
the fruit of the [alchemical] preparations, their origin,
[and] the elixir (<s>rasāyana</s>) for the body and metals.

body.translated_text: The twelve defects of <s>sūta</s> (mercury): ||1

body.text: teṣāṃ doṣāṇām apagamopāyaiḥ śuddhiṃ nirmalatāṃ tato'ṣṭādaśa pāṭasāraṇādīn saṃskārān pūrvaṃ vadāmi || 2
body.translated_text: The purification, i.e. the removal of those defects by the methods of removal, and then the eighteen processes (<s>saṃskāras</s>) beginning with cutting-and-liquefying (<s>pāṭasāraṇa</s>) — these I shall state first. ||2
Then the fruit of the processed preparations, in the form of the production of silver and so forth. ||3
Then the production of gold-line, tin-essence, and so forth. ||4

children.translated_text: * Then that which perfects the body,
* and that which perfects metals — [these are] the elixirs (<s>rasāyana</s>) — thus the statement of the disciple of Śrī <s>Kaṅkālaya</s>.

body.translated_text: In answer to what was promised, in order, he says: ||6

children.translated_text: One [defect is] the earthen sheath (<s>kañcuka</s>);
the second is the stone sheath;
the third is water-born;
and two each are born from lead (<s>nāga</s>) and tin (<s>vaṅga</s>).
<s>Kapālī</s> and <s>Kālikā</s> [are] from tin;
from lead, <s>Śyāmā</s> and <s>Kapālikā</s>.
Just as a film (<s>tarā</s>) [appears] in milk,
so are the two <s>Kapālikā</s> [defects] in appearance.
<s>Śyāmā</s> is of five colors;
<s>Kālikā</s> is black in color.
Mercury always has
seven innate sheaths (<s>kañcuka</s>).

body.translated_text: The three verses are clear. ||1
Only: 'two each from tin and lead' — ||2

body.text: iti dvau vaṅgajau doṣau dvau ca nāgajau || 3
body.translated_text: thus two defects from tin and two from lead. ||3
<s>Kapālī</s> and <s>Kālikā</s> are the fourth and fifth. ||4

body.text: vaṅgajau doṣau śyāmakapālikā ceti ṣaṣṭasaptamau nāgajau eteṣāṃ caturṇāṃ lakṣaṇamāha || 5
body.translated_text: The two from tin and <s>Śyāmā</s>-<s>Kapālikā</s> are the sixth and seventh, from lead. He states the characteristics of these four: ||5

body.text: dugdhe kvathite sati yādṛśī tarā upari bhavati || 6
body.translated_text: When milk is boiled, whatever film (<s>tarā</s>) appears on top — ||6
in mercury too, the tin-born [defect] is similar. ||7
And the lead-born <s>Kapālikā</s> appears on top. ||8

body.text: śyāmā ṣaṣṭo doṣaḥ pañcavarṇo bhavati kālikā ca pañcamo doṣaḥ kṛṣṇavarṇa iti || 9
body.translated_text: <s>Śyāmā</s>, the sixth defect, is five-colored, and <s>Kālikā</s>, the fifth defect, is black in color. ||9
Now he states the five defects of mercury: ||10

children.translated_text: One defect is that of impurity (<s>mala</s>);
the second is born of fire;
the third is the poison-defect;
the fourth is called pride (<s>darpa</s>).
The fifth defect is madness (<s>unmatta</s>) —
[these] five defects are always in mercury.

body.translated_text: The verse and a half are clear. ||1

body.text: atra ca jalamadhye mṛttikāpāṣāṇajalāntarasaṃyogāt tathā dugdhopari tarāvac ca ye dṛśyante te kañcukā ucyante || 2
body.translated_text: And here, those [impurities] that are seen amid water — from the conjunction of clay, stone, and water — and like a film on top of milk — these are called sheaths (<s>kañcuka</s>). ||2

body.text: ye punaḥ kodraveṣu madavadbhavanti te doṣā iti viśeṣaḥ || 3
body.translated_text: But those that are [present] in grains like <s>kodrava</s> as intoxicants — these are [called] defects. This is the distinction. ||3
Now he states the disorders caused by each of these defects: ||4

children.translated_text: From the earthen sheath,
skin disease (<s>kuṣṭha</s>) arises in embodied beings.
From the stone [sheath], stupor (<s>jāḍya</s>) arises;
and from the water-born [sheath], bloating of <s>Vāta</s>.
The tin-born and lead-born <s>Kapālikā</s> [sheaths]
produce scaly patches (<s>cilharī</s>) in the body.
<s>Kālikā</s> always produces
elephant-skin [disease] and ringworm (<s>dadrū</s>).
[The defects cause] pallor (<s>pāṇḍuroga</s>), delusion,
and also jaundice (<s>kāmalā</s>).
White leprosy (<s>śvetakuṣṭha</s>) arises
from the <s>Śyāmā</s>-sheath.
The impurity (<s>mala</s>) born in mercury
destroys the radiance of the body.
The fire-[defect] destroys the vital essence (<s>sattva</s>);
the poison[-defect] causes dizziness (<s>ghūrma</s>);
from the pride-[defect], the body breaks out [in eruptions];
from the madness-[defect], insanity (<s>unmatta</s>) results.
He who administers mercury
joined with twelve defects —
sins equal to the killing of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>
will always accrue to him.
He who administers the lord of mercury
freed from the twelve defects —
he will be exalted in this world
and will partake of heaven hereafter.
Freed from the twelve defects,
mercury makes the body free from disease.
Processed with processes numbering as the continents [i.e. seven or eighteen],
the processed [mercury] transforms both body and metals.

body.text: aṣṭāpi ślokāḥ spaṣṭā eva kevalaṃ cilharī kuṣṭhabheda eva || 1
body.translated_text: The eight verses are entirely clear. Only: <s>cilharī</s> is a type of skin disease (<s>kuṣṭha</s>). ||1
Thus the account of the defects and virtues of mercury is complete. ||2

children.translated_text: In mercury, there are eighteen processes (<s>saṃskāra</s>).
Of these, the first is cutting-and-liquefying (<s>pāṭasāraṇa</s>);
the second is called grinding (<s>mardana</s>);
the third is regarded as purification (<s>śodhana</s>).
The fourth is stupefaction-and-revival (<s>mūrchana-utthāpana</s>);
the fifth is precipitation of mercury (<s>rasapātana</s>);
the sixth is the revival (<s>utthāpana</s>) of mercury;
the seventh is steaming (<s>svedana</s>).
The eighth is declared as regulation (<s>niyāmaka</s>);
the ninth is confinement (<s>nirodhaka</s>);
the tenth is mouth-making (<s>mukhakārī</s>);
the eleventh (<s>Rudra</s>-number) is digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>).
The twelfth (<s>Sūrya</s>-number) is declared as fixation (<s>bandha</s>);
the thirteenth (<s>Yakṣa</s>-number) is liquefaction (<s>sāraṇa</s>);
the fourteenth (<s>Manu</s>-number) is killing (<s>māraṇa</s>);
the fifteenth (<s>Tithi</s>-number) is counter-liquefaction (<s>pratisāraṇa</s>).
The sixteenth is transmutation (<s>krāmaṇa</s>);
the seventeenth is penetration (<s>vedha</s>);
and the eighteenth process
is regarded by experts as unsealing (<s>udghāṭana</s>).

body.translated_text: The five verses are clear. ||1
These are the eighteen processes of mercury. ||2
Now, explaining the processes in order, he says: ||3

children.translated_text: When mercury is strained through cloth,
[that] process is cutting-and-liquefying (<s>pāṭasāraṇa</s>).
All the impurities born of tin, lead, and so forth
remain on the cloth.

body.text: prathamaṃ sūtaḥ ślakṣṇavastreṇa gālanīyo yathā vaṅganāgajāḥ pūrvoktavikārāḥ sarve vastre lagitvā tiṣṭhanti || 1
body.translated_text: First, mercury is to be strained through fine cloth, so that all the previously mentioned impurities born of tin, lead, etc. stick to and remain on the cloth. ||1
Thus the first process, <s>pāṭasāraṇa</s>, [is complete]. ||2

children.translated_text: To remove the blackness from mercury,
the [powder of] brick (<s>loṣṭajīkaka</s>) should be prepared.
One <s>pala</s> of that and
sixty-four <s>palas</s> of mercury —
placing [them] in a mortar, mixing,
one should grind for a <s>yāma</s> (three hours).
When ground, it becomes clear —
the blackness certainly departs.

body.text: ekaṃ palaṃ suniṣpannaśvetaloṣṭajīkakasya catuḥṣaṣṭipalāni ca pāradasyobhayaṃ saṃmelya khalve kṣiptvā praharamekaṃ mardayet || 1
body.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of well-prepared white brick-powder and sixty-four <s>palas</s> of mercury — mixing both and placing them in a mortar, one should grind for one <s>prahara</s> (three hours). ||1

body.text: yathā kālikāṃ tyaktvā nirmalībhavati pāradaḥ iti mardanasaṃskāro dvitīyaḥ || 2
body.translated_text: Such that, having shed the <s>Kālikā</s> [defect], the mercury becomes clear. Thus the second process, <s>mardana</s> (grinding). ||2

children.translated_text: Ground with the milk of <s>Vajrī</s> (<s>Snuhī</s>, spurge) for seven days,
the earthen [sheath] departs.
Ground with the milk of <s>Arka</s> (Calotropis) for seven days,
the stone sheath departs.

body.text: snuhīdugdhena khalve rasaḥ kṣiptvā sapta dināni mṛdyate || 1
body.translated_text: Mercury is placed in a mortar with the milk of <s>Snuhī</s> (spurge) and ground for seven days. ||1
Then the earthen sheath departs. ||2

body.text: evaṃ sapta dināni arkadugdhena mardite pāṣāṇakañcuko yāti || 3
body.translated_text: Likewise, when ground with the milk of <s>Arka</s> (Calotropis) for seven days, the stone sheath departs. ||3

children.translated_text: The bark-flakes of the <s>Brahmavṛkṣa</s> (Palāśa),
moistened with water, should be rolled [into a paste];
ground with its juice for seven days,
the water sheath departs.

body.text: palāśasya parpaṭān jalena kledayitvā tato vartayitvā vastreṇa niścotya raso grāhyaḥ || 1
body.translated_text: The bark-flakes of <s>Palāśa</s> should be soaked in water, then rolled into a paste, and the juice extracted through cloth. ||1

body.text: tena rasena sapta dināni raso mṛdyate || 2
body.translated_text: With that juice, the mercury should be ground for seven days. ||2
Such that the water-born sheath departs. ||3

children.translated_text: Ground with the decoction of <s>Citraka</s>,
the <s>Kapālī</s> [defect] born of tin departs.
Ground with the juice of <s>Vajrakanda</s>,
the <s>Kālikā</s> [defect] born of tin [departs].
Ground with the milk of <s>Kaṭutumbī</s> (bitter gourd),
the <s>Śyāmā</s> [defect] born of lead perishes.
Ground with the juice of <s>Bīya</s> (citron),
the <s>Kapālī</s> [defect] born of lead [departs].
By grinding for seven-times-seven days,
the sheaths perish from the mercury.

body.translated_text: The two and a half verses are clear. ||1

body.text: kevalaṃ vajraḥ snuhikandaś ca śūraṇas tayorasena || 2
body.translated_text: Only: <s>Vajra</s> is the <s>Snuhī</s> root-tuber, and <s>Śūraṇa</s> [is another name]; with the juice of these two. ||2

body.text: atha vā vajrākhyaḥ kandaḥ parvatabhūmau bhavati || 3
body.translated_text: Or alternatively: a tuber called <s>Vajra</s> grows on mountain-terrain. ||3

body.text: sarve'pi kañcukā yathoktarasena saptadināni sūtamardanena naśyantīti || 4
body.translated_text: All the sheaths are destroyed by grinding the mercury with the prescribed juice for seven days. ||4

children.translated_text: Ground with a decoction of <s>Triphalā</s>,
the impurity (<s>mala</s>) [defect] is thus destroyed.
Ground with a decoction of <s>Citraka</s>,
the fire-defect perishes.
Ground with the juice of <s>Aśvagandhā</s>,
the poison-defect is pacified.
Ground with the juice of <s>Nāhyā</s>,
the pride-defect is destroyed.
Ground with the juice of <s>Kudhya</s>,
even the madness[-defect] dissolves.
By grinding for seven-times-seven days,
the five defects are indeed destroyed.
Thus, freed from the twelve defects,
mercury becomes purified.

body.translated_text: [The three and a half verses are clear. ||1
Only: <s>Aśvagandhā</s> is <s>Āsandhi</s> (Withania somnifera). ||2]

children.translated_text: After each herb [treatment],
one should wash [the mercury] with sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>).
The purification of mercury (<s>sūta</s>)
should be performed with eleven medicines.

body.translated_text: And here is the traditional procedure: || 1
The juice of the prescribed medicine is placed upon the mercury (<s>rasa</s>) in the mortar (<s>khalva</s>). || 2

body.text: yathā yathā sūto bruḍati tathā tathā mardanīyaḥ || 3
body.translated_text: As the mercury becomes agitated (<s>bruḍati</s>), so should it be ground accordingly. || 3

body.text: śanaiḥ śanair yadi cāgretanauṣadharasaḥ śuṣyati tadā punaḥ kṣepaṇīyaḥ || 4
body.translated_text: If the juice of the previous medicine gradually dries up, then it should be added again. || 4

body.text: evaṃ saptadināni yadi marditaḥ pārado bhavati tadā kāñjikena kharalo bhriyate punaḥ śanairmṛdyate tato vastravartayaḥ kṣiptvā tathā mucyante tathā vartiprāntāḥ bhūmau laganti || 5
body.translated_text: Thus, if the mercury (<s>pārada</s>) has been ground for seven days, then the mortar is filled with sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>), and it is gently rubbed again; then cloth wicks are inserted and released such that the ends of the wicks touch the ground. || 5
Through these, the sour gruel filters and flows away. || 6

body.text: evaṃ sūtaḥ sarvair apyauṣadhaiḥ saptadināni piṣṭvā paścāt kāñjikena kṣālyaḥ || 7
body.translated_text: Thus, the mercury is ground with all the medicines for seven days each, and afterwards washed with sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>). || 7
And these eleven medicines are: || 8
<s>Vajrakṣīra</s> (spurge milk) || 9
<s>Arkakṣīra</s> (milkweed latex) || 10
<s>Palāśaparpaṭa</s> (butea leaf cake) || 11
<s>Citrakakvātha</s> (decoction of <s>Citraka</s>) || 12
<s>Vajrakanda</s> (spurge tuber) || 13
<s>Kaṭutumbā</s> (bitter gourd) || 14
<s>Bīaṅka</s> || 15
<s>Triphalākvātha</s> (decoction of three fruits) || 16
Again, <s>Citrakakvātha</s> (decoction of <s>Citraka</s>) || 17
<s>Aśvagandhā</s> (winter cherry) || 18
<s>Nāhi</s> || 19
<s>Aṅkudhya</s> || 20

body.text: atra citrakakvātho dvivelaṃ vidyate 'to dvādaśabhir auṣadhair ekādaśaiva iti sūtaśodhanasaṃskāras tṛtīyaḥ || 21
body.translated_text: Here, the decoction of <s>Citraka</s> occurs twice; therefore, with twelve medicines, there are indeed only eleven — thus the third <s>saṃskāra</s> (refinement) of mercury purification is complete. || 21

children.translated_text: With the decoction of <s>trikaṭu</s> (three pungents), the ground
naturally purified mercury (<s>rasa</s>)
is processed with the juice of <s>asannadūdhilī</s> (a spurge),
and also with the juice of fresh <s>ārdrā</s> (ginger),
and with the juice of <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade),
and with the juice of <s>devadālī</s>,
each time dried and ground again,
rubbing and pressing, one should dry it.
After each medicine,
one should wash it with sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>);
for each medicine, here
one should grind for seven days each.
The revival (<s>utthāpana</s>) of swooned (<s>mūrchita</s>) mercury
should be done with five medicines;
the mercury that has been swooned and revived
certainly becomes lustrous (<s>tejasvī</s>).

body.text: pūrvarītyā śodhitaḥ pāradaḥ khalve prathamaṃ trikaṭukvāthena pūrvavat saptadināni sampiṣya śoṣayet || 1
body.translated_text: The mercury purified by the previous method is first ground in the mortar with the decoction of <s>trikaṭu</s> (three pungents) for seven days as before, and then dried. || 1
Then it should be washed with sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>). || 2
Similarly, with the juice of <s>bhūmidūdhelī</s> (ground spurge), then with the juice of fresh ginger (<s>ārdra</s>). || 3
Next, with the juice of <s>karmāī</s> (black nightshade). || 4
Afterwards, with the juice of <s>devadālī</s>. || 5

body.text: sapta sapta dināni mṛditvā śoṣayitvā kāñjikena dhāvanīyaḥ || 6
body.translated_text: Grinding for seven days each, drying, and washing with sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>). || 6

body.text: evaṃ ca kṛte 'sau mūrchitotthitaḥ pārada ityucyate tejasvī ca bhavati || 7
body.translated_text: When done thus, that mercury is called 'swooned and revived' (<s>mūrchitotthita</s>) and becomes lustrous. || 7
Thus the fourth <s>saṃskāra</s>, the revival of swooned mercury (<s>mūrchitotthāpana</s>), is complete. || 8

children.translated_text: When the mercury attains the appearance of lampblack (<s>kajjala</s>),
having abandoned the fickleness of quicksilver,
it should then be known as swooned (<s>saṃmūrchita</s>);
sometimes it may also be of various colors.
One should then revive it by confining it
within a sealed vessel (<s>pātrasampuṭa</s>);
then one should swoon that mercury again,
and thereafter destroy its sheaths (<s>kañcukī</s>).
Thus, in this manner, step by step,
one should swoon it seven times;
mercury thus fully swooned
becomes free of defects (<s>doṣaśūnya</s>).

body.translated_text: Now, the revival according to another opinion: || 1

children.translated_text: The mercury should be revived
by the wise alchemist (<s>rasadhīmat</s>) with sour gruel (<s>āranāla</s>);
of the swooned-and-revived mercury,
sixty-four <s>palas</s> (units of weight),
and sixteen <s>palas</s> of copper powder —
place these in the mortar;
add lemon juice
and salt in the thirty-second part.
Grind it until
the paste (<s>pīṭhī</s>) becomes like an ointment (<s>mṛkṣaṇa</s>).

body.text: mūrchitotthitapāradasya palāni 64 sarvottamatāmracūrṇasya palāni 16 dvātriṃśattame bhāge lavaṇaṃ palāni 9 ityarthaḥ || 1
body.translated_text: 64 palas of swooned-and-revived mercury, 16 palas of the finest copper powder, salt in the thirty-second part = 2 palas — this is the meaning. || 1

body.text: sarva sarve ekīkṛtya nimbukarasena sammṛdya mṛkṣaṇopamā pīṭhī kāryā || 2
body.translated_text: Combining everything together, grinding with lemon juice, a paste like ointment should be made. || 2
Here is the traditional procedure: || 3

body.text: yāvanmātro rasastasya caturthe bhāge tāmracūrṇaṃ dvātriṃśattamabhāge lavaṇam || 4
body.translated_text: Whatever the quantity of mercury, its fourth part is copper powder, and the thirty-second part is salt. || 4

body.text: nimbukarasaś ca takhā kṣepyo yathā sarvamauṣadhaṃ majjati || 5
body.translated_text: Lemon juice should be added so that all the medicine is submerged. || 5

body.text: adhike doṣo nahi hīne tu doṣaḥ || 6
body.translated_text: Excess causes defects; but less does not cause defects. || 6
When dried, it should be added again. || 7

body.text: mardanaṃ ca tāvad yāvan mṛkṣaṇopamā pīṭhī || 8
body.translated_text: Grinding should continue until the paste becomes like ointment. || 8

children.translated_text: Having declared this, in the basin-receptacle (<s>kaṭāhabundha</s>)
one should place the cloth pouch (<s>vastrasampuṭa</s>);
the edges of the cloth should be smeared with clay
as if sealed to the receptacle.
Upon the mouth of a water-filled pot (<s>sthālikā</s>)
one should place the basin (<s>kaṭāha</s>) inverted;
the neck and the basin-joint
should likewise be sealed with cloth and clay.
Cow-dung cakes upon the basin —
one should burn them for half a <s>yāma</s> (watch, ~1.5 hours),
whereupon the mercury goes into the water below,
while the copper remains in the receptacle.
This should be done seven times;
this constitutes the pure distillation of mercury (<s>rasapātana</s>);
subtle defects are dissolved
in the swooned-revived distillation process.

body.text: ghaṭārdhasadṛśe kaṭāhe'dho mṛttikāyāḥ kuṇḍalī kāryate tac ca kaṭāhabundham ityucyate || 1
body.translated_text: In a basin resembling half a pot, a ring (<s>kuṇḍalī</s>) of clay is made at the bottom — this is called the basin-receptacle (<s>kaṭāhabundha</s>). || 1

body.text: tataḥ pūrvakṛtāṃ tāṃ pīṭhīṃ tatra kaṭāhabundhe kṣiptvopari ācchādanārthaṃ sabalacikkaṇavastrasampuṭaṃ tāḍayitvā tasya vastrasya prāntān kuṇḍalīṃ paritaś cikkaṇamṛdā tathā limpedyathā jaṭitā iva te bhaveyuḥ || 2
body.translated_text: Then, placing the previously made paste in that basin-receptacle, covering it above with a strong smooth cloth pouch, the edges of that cloth are smeared with smooth clay around the ring so that they become as if fused. || 2

body.text: tatastaṃ kaṭāhaṃ jalārdhapūrṇasthālikāmukhopari pradhvaraṃ muktvā sthālīkaṇṭhakaṭāhabundhakasaṃyogasthāne karpaṭamṛdaṃ dṛḍhaṃ dattvā kaṭāhamadhye chāṇakāni ghaṭīcatuṣkaṃ yāvaj jvālyante || 3
body.translated_text: Then, placing that basin inverted upon the mouth of the half-water-filled pot, applying cloth-and-clay firmly at the junction of the pot's neck and basin-receptacle, cow-dung cakes are burned in the middle of the basin for four <s>ghaṭīs</s> (about 1.5 hours). || 3
Then, by the heat of fire, the mercury exits through the holes in the cloth threads and enters the water situated in the pot below. || 4
The copper remains stuck to the bottom of the receptacle. || 5

body.text: tataḥ punarapi pūrvavat tāmracūrṇapāradapīṭhīṃ kṛtvā kaṭāhabundhasajalasthālikāyantreṇa pūrvavadraso jale pātyate || 6
body.translated_text: Then again, making the paste of copper powder and mercury as before, the mercury is dropped into water by the basin-and-water-pot apparatus as before. || 6

body.text: evaṃ saptavāraṃ rasapātane kṛte kuṇṭhatvajaḍatvādayaḥ sūkṣmadoṣā yānti || 7
body.translated_text: Thus, when the mercury distillation is done seven times, subtle defects such as dullness (<s>kuṇṭhatva</s>) and sluggishness (<s>jaḍatva</s>) are removed. || 7
Thus the fifth <s>saṃskāra</s>, the distillation of swooned-and-revived mercury (<s>pātanasaṃskāra</s>), is complete. || 8

children.translated_text: The mercury combined with the mortar
should be ground for three days;
then one should distill it as before,
downward, upward, and sideways.
Thus, with the distillation apparatus (<s>pātanayantra</s>),
one should distill it seven times;
mercury and mica (<s>abhra</s>) — the two should be ground
thoroughly with sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>).
In the middle of the bottom of the pot
that preparation, made into a ball, should be placed;
with <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), <s>rājikā</s> (mustard), <s>agni</s> (fire-plant),
<s>viṣa</s> (aconite), and <s>śigru</s> (drumstick) in equal parts,
smearing the upper pot
one should make a proper sealed vessel (<s>sampuṭa</s>);
at the joint, wrapping with clay,
the apparatus is the excellent <s>ḍamaru</s> (hourglass) apparatus.
On the upper part of this too
a ring (<s>kuṇḍalī</s>) should be fashioned;
beneath that, fire should be kindled,
gently, gently, for three watches (<s>triyāma</s>, ~9 hours).
Leaving the lower pot,
it migrates to the upper pot;
<s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol), <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), and mercury —
in equal amounts, for a day;
in the absence of <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol),
<s>phullatūrikā</s> (alum) should be used instead.
One should add little by little to the mortar
and grind the three together;
each should be one hundred <s>niṣkas</s> (weight units),
neither less nor ever more.
With the pot-seal apparatus (<s>sthālīsampuṭayantra</s>),
one should heat with intense fire for a day;
the mercury that adheres above
should be collected — it is pure and auspicious.
Taking thin leaves of copper, making a paste
with three times the mercury in a vessel,
From the copper, the mercury; from the mercury, the copper —
separated for the purpose of distillation;
the two, ground together again,
a paste should be made as before.
That paste of copper and mercury
should again be placed in the pot;
another pot placed face-down —
seal the mouth with cloth and clay.
This apparatus is called the <s>ḍamaruka</s> (hourglass)
and also known as <s>vidyādhara</s>;
on the receptacle of the upper pot,
cow dung should then be placed.
In the receptacle below the lower pot,
heat with gentle fire for one <s>yāma</s> (watch, ~3 hours);
the mercury rises to the upper pot,
while the copper remains right there.
This should be done seven times;
this is called the raising of mercury (<s>sūtotthāpana</s>);
the distilled and raised mercury becomes
pervasive (<s>vyāpaka</s>) and clear (<s>svaccha</s>).

body.text: pūrvasmin yoge pātanasaṃskārārthaṃ tāmrātsūtaḥ sūtāc ca tāmraṃ pṛthak saptavārakṛtam || 1
body.translated_text: In the previous recipe, the separation of mercury from copper and copper from mercury was done seven times for the purpose of the distillation <s>saṃskāra</s>. || 1

body.text: ihāpi yoge tadeva kariṣyate paraṃ tatra pātanāyehaiva pātitasyotthāpanāyeti viśeṣaḥ || 2
body.translated_text: In this recipe too, the same will be done; but the difference is that there it was for distillation, and here it is for the raising (<s>utthāpana</s>) of the distilled mercury. || 2
And it is as follows: || 3

body.text: rasapala66 tāmracūrṇapala16 lavaṇapala2 sarvaṃ nimbukarase mṛditvā pūrvavatpīṭhīṃ kṛtvā sthālikāyāṃ kṣiptvopari ca madhye mukhasthālīṃ dattvā dvayormukhayoge karpaṭamṛttikayā lipyate || 4
body.translated_text: 66 <s>palas</s> of mercury, 16 <s>palas</s> of copper powder, 2 <s>palas</s> of salt — all are ground in lemon juice, a paste is made as before, placed in the pot, and another pot placed above with mouth facing down; at the junction of the two mouths, it is sealed with cloth-and-clay. || 4

body.text: eṣa ḍamarukanāmā vidyādharanāmā ca yantra ucyate || 5
body.translated_text: This apparatus is called <s>ḍamaruka</s> and also <s>vidyādhara</s>. || 5

body.text: tato yā upari sthālī tasyā bundhe bāhyapārśve gomayaṃ dattvādhastanasthabundhādho yāmamātraṃ mṛduvahnir jvālanīyaḥ || 6
body.translated_text: Then, placing cow dung on the outer side of the receptacle of the upper pot, gentle fire should be kindled below the receptacle of the lower pot for one <s>yāma</s> (watch). || 6
Then the mercury flies upward and goes to the upper pot. || 7
The copper remains in the lower pot. || 8

body.text: evaṃ punaḥ punaḥ saptavāraṃ sūtotthāpane kṛte raso vyāpako bhavati || 9
body.translated_text: Thus, when the raising of mercury is done seven times repeatedly, the mercury becomes pervasive (<s>vyāpaka</s>). || 9
<s>Vyāpaka</s> means sharp (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) and having the nature of penetration (<s>prasaraṇaśīla</s>). || 10
Thus the sixth <s>saṃskāra</s>, the raising of distilled mercury (<s>utthāpanasaṃskāra</s>), is complete. || 11

children.translated_text: The leaves of the <s>Śigru</s> (drumstick) tree
should be rolled with water such that
a very soft ball is formed;
from the ball, one should make a cup (<s>kulhaḍī</s>).
The mercury raised after leaving the copper,
with salt in the thirty-second part,
should all be placed inside
the previously made cup (<s>kulhaḍī</s>).
One should place sour gruel (<s>āranāla</s>) in the pot,
along with juice from lemon;
a stick should be tied at the neck of the pot,
and the previously made cup bound in cloth to it.
The cloth should be tied to the stick
such that it does not touch the sour gruel;
with the pot thus sealed,
gentle fire should be kindled below.
For eight watches (<s>aṣṭayāma</s>, a full day) daily,
this should be done for seven days;
daily, with <s>Śigru</s> leaves,
a new cup (<s>kulhaḍikā</s>) should be made.
As the sour gruel evaporates,
fresh gruel should be added repeatedly;
by the swing apparatus (<s>dolāyantra</s>), the process
of steaming (<s>svedana</s>) of mercury should be performed.
Through steaming, fire is generated within;
the mercury becomes hungry (<s>bubhukṣita</s>, eager to absorb);
now, with its essence rising upward,
it tolerates fire during calcination (<s>vipācana</s>) exceedingly well.

body.text: śigrunāmno vṛkṣasya pattrāṇi gāḍhaṃ mṛkṣaṇopamānāni vartayitvā teṣāṃ piṇḍena kulhaḍīṃ kṛtvā tasyāṃ kulhaḍikāyāṃ pūrvavidhinā tāmraṃ parityajyodgīnaṃ rasaṃ tathā dvātriṃśattamena bhāgena lavaṇaṃ ca kṣiptvā tāṃ kulhaḍīṃ vastre baddhvā tadvastraṃ davarakeṇa kāṣṭhe baddhvā tatkāṣṭhaṃ sthālyāḥ kaṇṭhe kaṃcana paṭṭaṃ baddhvā sthālīmadhye tribhāganimbukarasasahitakāñjikaṃ kṣiptvā kāñjikopari ñūbamānā tathā vastraṃ baddhvā kulhaḍī moktavyā yathā kāñjikaṃ na lagati kevalaṃ bāṣpo lagati || 1
body.translated_text: Having firmly rolled the leaves of the tree called <s>Śigru</s> until they are like ointment, making a cup from their mass, placing in that cup the mercury extracted by the previous method after separating it from copper, along with salt in the thirty-second part, binding that cup in cloth, tying that cloth with a string to a stick, binding that stick at the neck of the pot with a strip, placing in the pot sour gruel combined with one-third lemon juice, releasing the cup bound in cloth hanging above the gruel so that the gruel does not touch it — only the steam touches it. || 1
Then fire should be kindled below the pot for a full day and night. || 2

body.text: tataḥ punarapi śigrupattrair navāṃ kulhaḍīṃ kṛtvā dolāyantreṇa tathaivāhorātraṃ rasaḥ svedanīyaḥ || 3
body.translated_text: Then, again making a new cup with <s>Śigru</s> leaves, the mercury should be steamed by the swing apparatus for a full day and night in the same way. || 3

body.text: yadi cāgretanaṃ kāñjikaṃ śuṣyati tathā punarnavaṃ kāñjikaṃ kṣepyam || 4
body.translated_text: If the previous sour gruel dries up, then fresh sour gruel should be added again. || 4

body.text: evaṃ saptabhirdinaiḥ saptabhiḥ kulhaḍībhiḥ saptavāraṃ svedito rasaḥ sampratyūrdhvaṃ pacyamāno 'tyarthamagniṃ sahate || 5
body.translated_text: Thus, the mercury steamed seven times over seven days with seven cups, now when calcined upward, tolerates fire exceedingly well. || 5
Thus the seventh <s>saṃskāra</s>, the steaming of raised mercury (<s>svedanasaṃskāra</s>), is complete. || 6
Steaming according to another text: || 7

children.translated_text: With <s>rājikā</s> (mustard), salt, <s>agni</s> (fire-plant) roots,
<s>rūṣaṇā</s> mixed with portions, in small pots,
of mercury, with gentle fire, this
steaming (<s>svedana</s>) is performed with husk-water (<s>tuṣajala</s>).
Within the medicinal leaves soaked in sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>),
suspended in the middle of a poultice (<s>poṭalī</s>),
that which is to be steamed is steamed over a hearth fire —
this is the swing apparatus (<s>dolāyantra</s>).
Making the cloth into a fourfold pouch,
also wrapped with a covering,
the mercury should be steamed over gentle fire
so that it does not undergo loss.
<s>Vyoṣa</s> (three pungents), fresh <s>Śigru</s> tuber,
<s>mayūramūlaka</s> (peacock radish), and <s>āsurī</s> (mustard) —
the mercury should be steamed with sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>)
by the wise one for a day.
The urines of cow, buffalo, and sheep,
and of donkey — these five urines,
with five salts and alkalis (<s>kṣāra</s>)
the lord of mercury (<s>raseśvara</s>) should be steamed.
<s>Cāṅgerī</s> (sorrel), sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>), lemon,
citron (<s>jambīra</s>), and <s>bījapūra</s> —
with these juices, mercury should be steamed
with the desire to open [its] mouth.
In the northern [direction], there should be a large
block of red rock-salt (<s>saindhava</s>).
Having made a cavity within it,
the steamed mercury should be placed [therein].
Then, having put <s>caṇaka</s> (chickpea) alkali [on top],
and above that, lemon
juice, one should place [the mercury] — a block of rock-salt
of similar [size] should be given [as a cover].
Having dug a pit in the earth
and placing the rock-salt sealed container [therein],
covering with eight finger-breadths of dust,
[burn] cow-dung fire for seven days.
Kindling the fire, it should be taken out
and washed with sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>).
This is the process called regulation (<s>niyāmaka</s>),
regarded as the eighth <s>saṃskāra</s>.
If the <s>caṇaka</s> alkali is exhausted,
the powder of <s>navasāra</s> (sal ammoniac) should be [used].
If the <s>sājī</s> alkali is exhausted,
then the alkali of <s>jhījaraṭa</s> [should be used].
<s>Hiṅgupūṣā</s> [should be used] if that is exhausted,
and likewise the fruits of castor (<s>eraṇḍa</s>).
Having put each <s>pūṣā</s> [alkali],
one should add lemon juice.
Extremely fire-resistant has become
that mercury — [it is now] regulated (<s>niyāmaka</s>).

body.text: annārthaṃ rasanā lolā niḥśaṅkaṃ saṃskṛtaḥ sadā || 1
body.translated_text: The tongue, eager for food, [that is] the well-processed [mercury] always moves about without hesitation. ||1

body.text: uttarasyāṃ diśi yaḥ sthūlo raktaḥ saindhavakhoṭako niṣpadyate || 2
body.translated_text: In the northern direction, the large red rock-salt block that is obtained — ||2

body.text: tasya madhyāt kīye chidraṃ ca vidhāya sveditaṃ rasaṃ tatra kṣiptvopari caṇakakṣāro deyastata upari svalpo nimbukarasaḥ kṣepyaḥ || 3
body.translated_text: having made a hole in its middle and placed the steamed mercury therein, <s>caṇaka</s> alkali should be put on top, and then a little lemon juice should be poured above. ||3

body.text: tatastasya chidrasyācchādanāyopari tādṛśa eva raktasaindhavakhoṭako deyaḥ || 4
body.translated_text: Then, to cover that hole, a similar red rock-salt block should be placed on top. ||4
And here is the understanding: ||5

body.text: yāvanmātraṃ chidramadhaḥkhoṭake bhavati tāvatī bhūmir dvitīyakhoṭakasya madhye muktvoparitaḥ kiṃcid utkīryate || 6
body.translated_text: Whatever the size of the hole in the lower block, that much of the surface of the second block's middle should be left, and above it, a little should be carved out. ||6
When the [second block] is placed on top, it becomes a rock-salt sealed container. ||7

body.text: tato bhūmau gajapramāṇāṃ gartāṃ kṛtvā tatra saindhavasampuṭaṃ muktvopary aṣṭāṅgulimānāṃ dhūliṃ dattvā chagaṇacūrṇena gartaṃ pūrayitvāgnir jvālanīyaḥ || 8
body.translated_text: Then, having dug an elephant-sized pit in the ground, placing the rock-salt container therein, covering with eight finger-breadths of dust, filling the pit with powdered cow-dung, the fire should be kindled. ||8

body.text: tataḥ prabhāte niṣkāsya kāñjikena prakṣālya punaḥ saindhavapuṭe kṣiptvopari navasāracūrṇaṃ nimbukarasaṃ ca muktvopari sampuṭaṃ ca dattvā punar gartāyāṃ muktvāhorātraṃ kārīṣāgnir jvālanīyaḥ || 9
body.translated_text: Then in the morning, taking it out, washing with <s>kāñjika</s>, again placing in the rock-salt container, putting <s>navasāra</s> powder and lemon juice above, giving the sealed cover, again placing in the pit, and kindling cow-dung fire for a day and night. ||9
Thus it should be processed seven times, [each] for seven days. ||10
On the third day, <s>sājī</s> alkali [is used]. ||11
On the fourth day, <s>jhījarīṭa</s> alkali. ||12
On the fifth day, <s>hiṅgupuṣā</s>; on the sixth and seventh days, castor fruit powder. ||13
Above all [of them], lemon juice is to be added. ||14
When done thus, the regulated mercury becomes extremely fire-resistant. ||15
And [the mercury], slightly rising, hungry, moves its tongue [i.e. becomes active]. ||16
Thus the regulation (<s>niyāmaka</s>) process of steamed mercury — the eighth. ||17

children.translated_text: In a glass vessel (<s>kācakumpa</s>), smear with clay;
in the middle, place the regulated mercury;
having tied cloth at the mouth
and covered with a <s>koḍīyaka</s> (clay lid),
placing the vessel in a pit in the ground,
and putting sand on top —
one should kindle cow-dung fire daily
for seven days.
The mercury should be taken from the vessel —
[this] is the prescribed confinement (<s>nirodhaka</s>) [process].
Licking its tongue
and tormented by extreme hunger,

body.text: kācakumpikāyāṃ cikkaṇāṃ mṛdaṃ dattvā madhye niyāmakaṃ rasaṃ kṣiptvā mukhe koḍīyakam || 1
body.translated_text: In a glass vessel, having put smooth clay and placed the regulated mercury in the middle, at the mouth [place] a <s>koḍīyaka</s>. ||1
What is the meaning? A clay saucer should be placed. ||2
On top, having put cloth and clay, it should be dried. ||3

body.text: tato bhūmau gajapramāṇāṃ gartāṃ kṛtvā tatra kṣiptvopari aṣṭāṅgulidhūliṃ dattvāhorātraṃ kārīṣāgnirjvālanīyaḥ || 4
body.translated_text: Then, having dug an elephant-sized pit in the ground, placing [the vessel] therein, covering with eight finger-breadths of dust above, and kindling cow-dung fire for a day and night. ||4

body.text: tataḥ punaḥ prabhāte rakṣāṃ kṛtvā navaṃ chagaṇacūrṇaṃ kṣiptvāhorātraṃ ca kārīṣāgnirjvālanīyaḥ || 5
body.translated_text: Then again in the morning, having performed the protection [ritual], putting fresh cow-dung powder, and kindling cow-dung fire for a day and night. ||5

body.text: evaṃ saptabhir dinaiḥ saptavāraṃ saṃskṛto'sau nirodhako nāma raso mahābubhukṣayā pīḍito jihvāṃ lelihyamānaḥ kumpito grāhyaḥ || 6
body.translated_text: Thus, processed seven times over seven days, this mercury, called <s>nirodhaka</s> (confined), tormented by great hunger, licking its tongue, should be taken from the vessel. ||6
Thus the confinement (<s>nirodhaka</s>) process of the regulated mercury — the ninth. ||7

children.translated_text: <s>Snuhī</s>, <s>Girikarṇī</s>,
<s>Kṣīriṇī</s>, <s>Vajrakañcukī</s>,
<s>Sarpākṣī</s>, <s>Meghanādā</s>,
<s>Matsyākṣī</s>, <s>Mṛgabhojanī</s>,
<s>Śiraḥpuṅkhā</s>, <s>Cāṅgerī</s>,
<s>Vajravastrī</s>, <s>Punarnavā</s>,
<s>Madhukaṃsārī</s>, <s>Tiktā</s>,
<s>Trāyantī</s>, <s>Candana</s>, <s>Amṛtā</s>,
<s>Āraṇyatulasī</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>,
<s>Śākhinī</s>, <s>Ravibhūlikā</s> —
these are declared as regulators (<s>niyāmikā</s>)
in mercury procedures, by <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva).
Of these regulators,
one should use whichever is available.
One would certainly become wing-clipped [i.e. powerless]
[without] the herb, by the ripening of merit.
Now I declare the regulators
for the killing (<s>māraṇa</s>) procedure of mercury:
<s>Sarpākṣī</s>, <s>Kṣīriṇī</s>, <s>Vadhyā</s>,
<s>Matsyākṣī</s>, <s>Śaṅkhapuṣpikā</s>,
<s>Kākajaṅghā</s>, <s>Śikhiśikhā</s>,
<s>Brahmadaṇḍī</s>, <s>Ākhuparṇikā</s>,
<s>Varṣābhū</s>, <s>Kañcukī</s>, <s>Mūrvā</s>,
<s>Mācīka</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Ciñcikā</s>,
<s>Śatāvarī</s>, <s>Dvilatā</s>,
<s>Vajrakanda</s>, <s>Ādikarṇikā</s>,
<s>Maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>, <s>Pāṭhālī</s>,
<s>Citraka</s>, <s>Grīṣmasandara</s>,
<s>Kākamācī</s>, <s>Mahārāṣṭrī</s>,
<s>Haridrā</s>, <s>Tilaparṇikā</s>,
white <s>Arka</s>, <s>Śigru</s>, <s>Dhattūra</s>,
<s>Mṛgadūrvā</s>, <s>Harītakī</s>,
<s>Guḍūcī</s>, <s>Musalī</s>, <s>Puṅkhā</s>,
<s>Bhṛṅgarāja</s>, red <s>Citraka</s>,
<s>Nāraṅga</s>, <s>Sūraṇa</s>, <s>Muṇḍī</s>,
pigeon-excrement (<s>mala</s>), <s>Kāpotakokila</s>,
rock-salt (<s>saindhava</s>), white <s>Varṣābhū</s>,
tin (<s>khāpara</s>), <s>hiṅgu</s>, pyrites (<s>mākṣika</s>),
<s>Viṣṇukrāntā</s>, <s>Somavallī</s>,
<s>Brahmaghnī</s>, <s>Yakṣalocanā</s>,
<s>Vyāghrapādī</s>, <s>Haṃsapādī</s>,
<s>Vṛścikālī</s>, <s>Kutumbaka</s>,
<s>Svayībhuk</s>, <s>Kusama</s>, <s>Kumbhī</s>,
<s>Hastiśuṇḍī</s>, <s>Indravāruṇī</s>,
and the seeds of <s>Arūṣkara</s> (marking nut) —
all these are regulators (<s>niyāmikā</s>).
These, all together or individually,
should be given — more than seventeen.
In the killing, stupefaction, and fixation
of mercury, these should be employed —
ground with the urine of unbred cows,
<s>Mūrvā</s> [serves as] a regulator.
With those fluids, one should grind the mercury
in the manner previously stated, in order.
Thus, the killing (<s>māraṇa</s>) conjoined with
digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>) is declared.
Taking a good stalk of <s>bījapūra</s> (citron),
pull it out and make a cavity.
The confined (<s>nirodhaka</s>) [mercury] with salt
should be placed inside and covered with it.
A pot filled with <s>kāñjika</s>
and saturated with the juice of lemons —
by a swing-apparatus (<s>dolāyantra</s>), in that [pot],
the <s>bījapūra</s> submerged up to [the neck] —
having tied and covered, for seven days
strong fire (<s>haṭhāgni</s>) should be kindled below.
Daily, with fresh citrons,
the face [of the mercury] should be renewed.
It devours mica (<s>abhraka</s>) and such things;
when the mouth of the mercury is opened,
with wide-open mouth it devours
everything that is placed [before it], and all is digested.

body.text: suniṣpannabījapūrasya vṛntam utpāṭya madhye utkīrya chidraṃ kṛtvā tato nirodhakaṃ rasaṃ kṣiptvopari lavaṇaṃ muktvā punastena vṛntena chādayitvā bījapūrakaṃ vastre baddhvā tribhāgena nimbukarasayuktakāñjikabhṛtasthālī madhye dolāyantreṇa pūrvoktena kāñjike bruḍantaṃ bījapūrakaṃ dhṛtvādho 'gnir jvālanīyo 'horātram || 1
body.translated_text: Having pulled out the stalk of a well-ripened <s>bījapūra</s>, carved out the middle and made a cavity, then placed the confined mercury therein, put salt on top, covered again with that stalk, tied the <s>bījapūra</s> in cloth, and held it submerged in a pot one-third filled with <s>kāñjika</s> mixed with lemon juice by means of the previously described swing-apparatus — fire should be kindled below for a day and night. ||1

body.text: tataḥ punaḥ prabhāte navaṃ bījapūrakamānīya tathaiva madhye rasaṃ kṣiptvā dolāyantreṇāhorātraṃ rasaḥ saṃskāryaḥ || 2
body.translated_text: Then again in the morning, bringing a fresh <s>bījapūra</s>, similarly placing the mercury in the middle, and by means of the swing-apparatus, the mercury should be processed for a day and night. ||2

body.text: evaṃ saptabhir dinaiḥ saptavāraṃ navanavair mātuluṅgaiḥ saṃskṛto raso dhānyābhrakādīnāṃ grasanāya prasāritamukho vidhinā dattaṃ sarvaṃ grāsaṃ jīryati || 3
body.translated_text: Thus, processed seven times over seven days with fresh citrons each time, the mercury, with its mouth opened for the devouring of grain-mica and such, devours in the prescribed manner all food that is given [to it] and digests it. ||3
Thus the mouth-opening (<s>mukhaprasāraṇa</s>) process of the confined mercury — the tenth. ||4

children.translated_text: With <s>Karkoṭī</s>, <s>Phaṇinetrā</s>,
<s>Viñcikā</s>, <s>Ambuja</s>, and <s>Mārkava</s> —
it should be regulated, and then properly
the fickleness should be removed.

Tormented by the processes of grinding, stupefaction, and precipitation, [the mercury] becomes of weak potency; / by the lotuses of creation [i.e. specific herbs] and from confinement, it becomes approximately like two flat surfaces — not granular. //

children.text: sṛṣṭyāmbujair nirodhāt taladvayaprāyo na khaṇḍaḥ syāt //
children.translated_text: [continued from above]
Thus tormented in body, with its own potency drained,

children.text: sṛṣṭyāṃ citaś chagaṇakaiḥ puṭito valī syāt
children.translated_text: arranged on [a surface] of creation, pelletized with cow-dung cakes, heated in a crucible, it becomes wrinkled.
Steamed with powders of borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), pepper (<s>uṣaṇa</s>), <s>Svayā</s>, mustard (<s>suri</s>), and <s>Śigru</s>,
for three days in barley-water, it then becomes fully ignited (<s>sudīpta</s>).
<s>Triphalā</s>, <s>Citramūla</s> (the root of <s>Citraka</s>),
<s>Saurāṣṭrī</s> (alum), and <s>Navasādara</s> (sal ammoniac) —
mixing with the juice of <s>Śigru</s>,
one should grind for three days.
With that very [mixture], placing [mercury] in the middle,
it should be regulated again and again.
When the thirteenth day arrives,
the auspicious ignition (<s>dīpana</s>) occurs.
With borax, realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>), salt, mustard (<s>āsuri</s>), <s>Śigru</s>, and <s>kāñjika</s>, for three days / by steaming, the dimly-ignited [mercury] becomes food-seeking. //
[continued from above]

body.text: iti dīpto viśuddhaḥ prabalataravidyucchaṭāsahasrābhaḥ sutarāṃ bhavati || 1
body.translated_text: Thus the ignited [mercury], purified, resembling a thousand flashes of exceedingly powerful lightning, becomes [ready]. ||1
The lord of mercury should also be employed in medicinal elixir (<s>rasāyana</s>) preparations. ||2
Thus [end] the passages on ignition (<s>dīpana</s>). ||3

children.translated_text: The filled glass vessel —
salt, lemon juice,
placing one <s>pala</s> of grain-mica (<s>dhānyābhraka</s>),
smear the mouth with cloth and clay.
At the mouth, give a <s>koḍīyaka</s> (clay lid);
a pot filled with sand —
placing the vessel amidst the sand
and putting sand on top,
giving [fuel] below, for eight <s>yāmas</s> (24 hours),
the wise one should kindle strong fire.
One <s>pala</s> of grain-mica
is to be digested (<s>jāraṇa</s>) day and night.
Eight times the weight of the mercury should be digested —
grain-mica, by the knower of mercury.
By name, this is called the 'sky-devourer'
(<s>gaganagrāsa</s>) mercury.

body.text: kācakumpikāmadhye prasāritamukhaṃ rasaṃ palam ekaṃ madhye muktvā kumpikāmukhe cātikāṃ dattvopari karpaṭamṛttikayā liptvā śoṣayet || 1
body.translated_text: In the middle of a glass vessel, having placed one <s>pala</s> of the mouth-opened mercury, putting a clay saucer at the vessel's mouth, and sealing it above with cloth and clay, it should be dried. ||1

body.text: tataḥ pṛthulamukhāyāṃ kuṇḍikāyāṃ vālukāṃ kṣiptvopari aṅgula 4 || 2
body.translated_text: Then, in a wide-mouthed pot, placing sand above, four or ||2

body.text: pañcapramāṇāṃ dhūliṃ dattvā kuṇḍikāyā adho 'ṣṭayāmān haṭhāgniṃ jvālayitvā dhānyābhrakapalaṃ jāraṇīyam || 3
body.translated_text: five finger-breadths of dust, and kindling strong fire below the pot for eight <s>yāmas</s>, one <s>pala</s> of grain-mica should be digested. ||3
And here is the traditional instruction: ||4

body.text: kuṇḍikāyāṃ tathā vālukā kṣepyā yathā tasyā upari kumpikāyāṃ muktāyāṃ tadupari aṅgula 4 || 5
body.translated_text: Sand should be placed in the pot such that when the vessel is placed upon it, ||5

body.text: pañcapramāṇāyāṃ vālukāyāṃ kṣiptāyāṃ kuṇḍikā pūrṇā bhavati || 6
body.translated_text: with four or five finger-breadths of sand placed above [the vessel], the pot becomes full. ||6

body.text: tathā rasapala 64 lavaṇapala 2 dhānyābhrakapala 1 iti mātrāpramāṇam || 7
body.translated_text: And the proportions are: 64 <s>palas</s> of mercury, 2 <s>palas</s> of salt, 1 <s>pala</s> of grain-mica. ||7

body.text: tatastāṃ kumpīm bhaṅktvā rasaṃ gṛhītvā punarapi dvitīyakumpikāyāṃ rasadhānyābhrakalavaṇanimbukarasān kṣiptvā pūrvavadahorātraṃ haṭhāgnijvālanena dhānyābhrakapalaṃ jāraṇīyam || 8
body.translated_text: Then, breaking that vessel, taking the mercury, and again in a second vessel, placing mercury, grain-mica, salt, and lemon juice, and as before, kindling strong fire for a day and night, one <s>pala</s> of grain-mica should be digested. ||8

body.text: evamaṣṭabhir dinair aṣṭabhiḥ kumpikābhir aṣṭadhānyābhrakapalāni jāraṇīyāni || 9
body.translated_text: Thus, in eight days, with eight vessels, eight <s>palas</s> of grain-mica should be digested. ||9
Then this mercury is called 'sky-devourer' (<s>gaganagrāsa</s>). ||10

children.translated_text: All the mica, rendered into a single sheet,
thereafter —
placed on a heated iron pan,
it should be burned with intense fire.
With the water of <s>Agastya</s>-flowers
and with the juice of water-lilies (<s>kumuda</s>),
with <s>Varṣābhū</s>-<s>Tundalī</s> [juice],
with pepper (<s>marica</s>) and good-faced [substance] —
with buffalo milk,
having liquefied the mica, then
flooding with barley-<s>vicchikā</s> water,
it should be heated in a crucible.
With pepper, mustard, white mustard,
and poison-powders, the mercury
should be steamed, bound in <s>kāñjika</s>,
in a swing-apparatus for three days.
The mercury thus steamed, then
in <s>kāñjika</s>, the barley-<s>vicchikā</s>
with roots and leaves, having gathered
and combined — the discerning one —
in <s>kāñjika</s> it comes to be, O goddess,
in the fixation of mercury, constantly.
For gold, the gold-face procedure [is used];
for silver, the silver-face is made.
With barley-<s>vicchikā</s> water
the wise one should steam again and again.
At the tip of the metal, revolving, the <s>Śāla</s> [resin],
well-burned, should be likewise applied.
The sign of digestion should be known:
[mercury] that bears [the shape of] a leech-staff.
In the second [stage], it resembles crow-excrement;
in the third, it becomes oily.
Then tawny, without belching,
it does not release sparks.
When smelt on fire, it settles —
this is the sign of sky-digestion.
Then, from the touch of a transformative substance,
toward the face of the divine herb —
then it moves swiftly,
and in an instant it is fixed.
Then, placed on a metal pan,
it should be steamed with mild fire.
With warm sour gruel (<s>aranāla</s>),
the wise one [washes] the washed mercury.
Thus, of the mica-digested mercury,
one-eighth [of the weight] —
<s>viḍa</s> (a specific salt preparation) should be given according to procedure
the wise one should cause it to be digested.
Thus, having been digested with six times [its weight of mica],
the wise one should cause the mercury to be digested.
That which quickly adheres to the ground
is called <s>dhānyābhraka</s> (grain-mica).
When twice [its weight of] mica has been digested,
it moves away by means of smoke.
When four times [its weight] has been digested in it,
the power of movement is impaired.
Leaping up again and again, outside
it certainly falls from the crucible.
When six times [its weight] has been digested, the mercury
trembles repeatedly.
It does not fly away outside,
remaining in its place, it becomes steady.
When eight times [its weight] has been digested in it,
the mercury, when heated, becomes calm.
Even when forcefully heated by fire,
it becomes like solidified gold.
By anointing silver coins with this
and filtering them,
gold of ten <s>varṇa</s> (purity grades) is produced --
so say those who know <s>rasa</s> (mercury/alchemy).

body.translated_text: Here is the traditional procedure: ||1

body.text: pūrvam abhrakair akhaṇḍavrīhibhiḥ ślakṣṇapāṣāṇakarkarair vādṛḍhanahīnavastrako thalikāṃ bhṛtvā dvāraṃ davarakeṇa dṛḍhaṃ baddhvā kāṣṭhapattrikāyāṃ jalapūrṇāyāṃ muktvā gāḍhaṃ tathā mardanīyo yathābhrakaṃ cūrṇībhūya kiṃcid bahir niḥsarati || 2
body.translated_text: First, having filled a cloth bag -- free from thick and loose cloth -- with mica, unbroken rice grains, and smooth stone pebbles, tying the opening firmly with a plug, and placing it in a wooden trough filled with water, one should grind vigorously so that the mica, having become powder, gradually comes out. ||2
And having dried that, the fine powder is collected. ||3

body.text: idaṃ ca bhūmikāyāṃ kṣiptaṃ sūkṣmatvāt tatra lagati || 4
body.translated_text: And this, when thrown upon the ground, adheres there due to its fineness. ||4
Those who know <s>rasa</s> (mercury) call this <s>dhānyābhraka</s> (grain-mica). ||5

body.text: tathā pāradādviguṇe dhānyābhrakeṇa jīrṇe'gniṃ tāpayettato raso dhūmena kṛtoḍḍīya yāti || 6
body.translated_text: Then, when twice [the weight of] mercury in <s>dhānyābhraka</s> has been digested, if one heats with fire, the mercury flies away having risen up by means of smoke. ||6

body.text: caturguṇe dhānyābhrake jīrṇe dhūmarūpeṇa na yāti || 7
body.translated_text: When four times [its weight of] <s>dhānyābhraka</s> has been digested, it does not go away in the form of smoke. ||7

body.text: kiṃtu haṭhāgniyoge mūṣāyām uḍḍīya bahiḥ patati || 8
body.translated_text: However, with forceful application of fire, it flies up in the crucible and falls outside. ||8

body.text: ṣaḍguṇe dhānyābhrake jīrṇe bahiruḍḍīya na yāti || 9
body.translated_text: When six times [its weight of] <s>dhānyābhraka</s> has been digested, it does not fly away outside. ||9
However, it trembles within the crucible. ||10

body.text: aṣṭaguṇe jīrṇe haṭhena dhmāto hi suvarṇavat sthirībhavati na punaḥ punarmanāgapi kampate || 11
body.translated_text: When eight times [its weight] has been digested, even when forcefully heated, it becomes steady like gold and does not tremble even the slightest bit anymore. ||11

body.text: tato mahāgnisahena tena rasena rūpyagadyāṇakapattram abhyañjya gālyate || 12
body.translated_text: Then, with that mercury which withstands great fire, having anointed a silver coin-leaf and filtering it. ||12
Then it becomes gold of ten <s>varṇa</s> (purity grade) -- gold indeed. ||13

body.text: iti prasārite mukhasya rasasya gaganagrāsajāraṇaṃ prathamam || 14
body.translated_text: Thus, in the expanded [commentary], the first [procedure] is the <s>gaganagrāsa-jāraṇa</s> (sky-devouring digestion) of <s>mukha-rasa</s> (mouth-mercury). ||14

children.translated_text: The leaves of mica,
finely powdered,
should be ground for three days
with the juice of cotton-plant.
Also with the juice of <s>mātuliṅga</s> (citron)
and <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) water, one should grind,
adding <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) alkali
and likewise <s>navasāra</s> (sal ammoniac).
Then, having placed [the mercury] in a mortar,
one should grind it daily
with the previously mentioned juices, repeatedly,
until it clearly swallows [the mica].
<s>Yava</s> (barley), plantain, <s>śigru</s> (drumstick tree),
<s>ciñcā</s> (tamarind) fruit, <s>punarnava</s> (Boerhavia),
<s>śatamūlī</s> (Asparagus) -- with these juices, the mica
should be treated a sage's number [of times] (seven).
That king of <s>rasa</s> (mercury) [then] easily
devours this morsel when the excellent mouth
has been created, for the purpose of bodily perfection
and indeed for the perfection of metals.
If the mercury accepts
even a small amount of mica comfortably,
it becomes bound within its own house,
like a very restless thief.
<s>Kumārī</s> (Aloe vera), plantain, <s>vajrī</s> (Euphorbia),
<s>jārī</s>, <s>hemapādī</s>, <s>naṭī</s>,
<s>bṛhatī</s> (Solanum), <s>agnidamanī</s>,
<s>lāṅgalī</s> -- in equal parts.
Leaf-mica or mica powder (wild),
treated an equal number of times with impurity-[removing agents],
with heated iron powder --
a paste is formed when ground into the mercury.
In a four-footed iron mortar,
one should place mercury that has swallowed mica,
with a one-sixty-fourth part
of <s>kānta</s> (magnetic) iron powder relative to the mercury.
Moistened with sour gruel,
<s>bavvera</s> (impure copper sulphate) and <s>thūthaka</s> (copper vitriol) --
that is called <s>viḍa</s> (auxiliary salt)
and <s>candana</s> (sandalwood) by those who know <s>rasa</s>.
Grinding with <s>thūthā-viḍa</s> (vitriol-salt),
one should kindle a mild fire below.
Eight times the mercury's [weight] of iron
should always be digested by the wise.
If <s>kānta</s> (magnetic) iron is unavailable,
one should use powder of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (sharp/steel) iron,
one-sixty-fourth part [at a time],
adding repeatedly as each is digested.
That mercury, having digested the iron,
becomes wheat-colored and astringent,
bound and capable of withstanding coloring --
the color too is digested.

body.text: yasmin lohakhalve catvāraḥ pādā mañcikayābhibhavanti sa catuṣpāda ucyate || 1
body.translated_text: The iron mortar in which four feet are joined by a frame is called 'four-footed.' ||1

body.text: tasmin lohakhalve grastābhrakasūtaṃ tathā catuḥṣaṣṭitamena sūtakasya kāntalohacūrṇaṃ kṣiptvā yathā viḍena saha loṣṭikayā mandaṃ mandaṃ mandaṃ mardayet || 2
body.translated_text: In that iron mortar, the mercury that has swallowed mica, together with one-sixty-fourth [part] of <s>kānta</s> iron powder relative to the mercury, having been placed, should be ground very gently with the <s>viḍa</s> (auxiliary salt) using a pestle. ||2
And a gentle fire should be kindled below. ||3

body.text: evaṃ kurvatā yadi kāntalohacūrṇacatuḥṣaṣṭitamo jīrṇo bhavati tadā punarapi catuḥṣaṣṭitamabhāgena kāntalohacūrṇaṃ kṣiptvā thūthāviḍena peṣaṇīyam || 4
body.translated_text: While doing thus, if the one-sixty-fourth [part] of <s>kānta</s> iron powder is digested, then again, having added a one-sixty-fourth part of <s>kānta</s> iron powder, it should be ground with <s>thūthā-viḍa</s> (vitriol-salt). ||4
And fire should be kindled below. ||5

body.text: evaṃ pūrvakṣipte lohacūrṇe jīrṇe punaḥ punas tāvac catuḥṣaṣṭitamāṃśena lohacūrṇaṃ kṣepyam || 6
body.translated_text: Thus, when the previously added iron powder is digested, again and again, a one-sixty-fourth part of iron powder should be added, ||6
until eight times the mercury's [weight] of iron powder is digested. ||7

body.text: ityarthaṃ lohacūrṇasya kaṣāyeṇa rasaḥ pāśitaḥ san godhūmavarṇo bhavati || 8
body.translated_text: For this purpose: the mercury, bound by the astringency of iron powder, becomes wheat-colored. ||8
And it also withstands coloring. ||9
Then the coloring agents like <s>prakāśa</s> (bright) etc. are also digested. ||10

body.text: atra ca yadi kāntalohaṃ na labhyate tadā tīkṣṇāyasaṃ sāralohac || 11
body.translated_text: And here, if <s>kānta</s> (magnetic) iron is not obtainable, then <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (steel) iron, i.e. <s>sāra</s> (core) iron [should be used]. ||11

body.text: tathāya tvagheraṃ thūthakaṃ tat kāñjikena saṃghṛṣya candanaṃ kṣipyate || 12
body.translated_text: Similarly, <s>tvagheraṃ thūthaka</s> (copper vitriol), that is rubbed with sour gruel and <s>candana</s> (sandalwood) is added. ||12
This is called <s>thūthā-viḍa</s> (vitriol-salt). ||13
Hereafter too, wherever the term <s>thūthā-viḍa</s> appears, this same [substance] should be understood. ||14
Thus the second [procedure] is the iron-digestion of mercury that has swallowed mica. ||15

children.translated_text: In a four-footed iron mortar,
one should place iron-digested mercury,
and <s>ayaḥprakāśa</s> (bright iron / iron pyrite) and <s>rāji</s> (streak / galena)
as powder in one-sixty-fourth part.
Grinding with <s>thūthā-viḍa</s> (vitriol-salt),
one should kindle a mild fire below.
Eight times the mercury's [weight] of <s>rāji</s> (galena)
and <s>ayaḥprakāśa</s> (iron pyrite) should be digested.
When <s>ayaḥprakāśa-rāji</s> (iron pyrite and galena)
has been digested, yellowness is produced.
For the purpose of producing redness,
one should digest <s>himarāji</s> (gold-streak / gold ore).

body.text: pūrvokte ca catuṣpāde lohakhalve jīrṇalohaṃ rasaṃ tathā || 1
body.translated_text: In the aforementioned four-footed iron mortar, [place] the iron-digested mercury; likewise ||1

body.text: catuḥṣaṣṭitamabhāgena ayaḥprakāśirājicūrṇaṃ ca kṣiptvā pūrvoktena thūthāviḍena mardayet || 2
body.translated_text: having added a one-sixty-fourth part of <s>ayaḥprakāśa-rāji</s> (iron pyrite and galena) powder, one should grind with the previously mentioned <s>thūthā-viḍa</s>. ||2
And a gentle fire should be kindled below. ||3

body.text: agretanakṣiptāyaḥprakāśaṃ cūrṇe ca jīrṇe punas tāvan mātramayaḥ || 4
body.translated_text: When the previously added <s>ayaḥprakāśa</s> (iron pyrite) powder is digested, again that same amount of iron [pyrite]... ||4

body.text: evaṃ ca yadi rasād aṣṭaguṇāyaḥprakāśarājijīrṇā bhavati || 5
body.translated_text: Thus, if eight times the mercury's [weight] of <s>ayaḥprakāśa-rāji</s> is digested, ||5
Then the mercury becomes yellow. ||6

body.text: tataḥ sūtasya raktatānimittaṃ vakṣyamāṇarītyā hemarājiṃ jārayet || 7
body.translated_text: Then, for the purpose of making the mercury red, one should digest <s>hemarāji</s> (gold-streak ore) by the method to be described. ||7
Thus the third [procedure] is the digestion of <s>ayaḥprakāśa-rāji</s> (iron pyrite and galena) in iron-digested mercury. ||8

body.text: rājisvarūpaṃ cāgre svayaṃ sa ca vyākhyāsyati || 9
body.translated_text: And the nature of <s>rāji</s> (galena/streak), he himself will explain later. ||9

children.translated_text: In a four-footed iron mortar,
the mercury in which <s>ayaḥprakāśa</s> (iron pyrite) has been fully digested,
and <s>hemarāji</s> (gold-streak ore) --
as powder in one-sixty-fourth part.
Grinding with <s>thūthā-viḍa</s> (vitriol-salt),
one should kindle a mild fire below.
Eight times the mercury's [weight] of <s>hemarāji</s>
(gold-streak ore) should be digested by the experts.
When the <s>hemarāji</s> (gold-streak ore)
has been digested, redness is certainly produced.
For the purpose of producing gold,
purified <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) should indeed be digested.

body.translated_text: Just as the digestion of <s>ayaḥprakāśa-rāji</s> (iron pyrite and galena) was [described], so too the digestion of <s>hemarāji</s> (gold-streak ore) should be understood. ||1
Eight times the mercury's [weight] -- the rest is clear. ||2
Thus the fourth [procedure] is the digestion of <s>hemarāji</s> in mercury that has digested <s>ayaḥprakāśa-rāji</s>. ||3

children.translated_text: A pit made of clay lumps, plastered with lime,
[or] with powder mixed with <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery),
thickly plastered and self-dried --
this apparatus is considered the <s>bhūdhara</s> (earth-holder) device.
The mercury in which <s>hemarāji</s> (gold-streak ore) has been digested,
[placed] in the <s>bhūdhara</s> (earth-holder) apparatus,
together with a one-sixteenth part
of purified <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) powder.
At the mouth, a <s>koḍīyaka</s> (small cup) should be placed
face-down as a lid.
It should be sealed with cloth and clay,
and then a strong fire should be kindled.
A one-sixteenth part should be given repeatedly,
and likewise the <s>koḍīyaka</s> [renewed] each time,
until six times the mercury's [weight]
of purified <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) is digested.
Firmness and color are produced
when <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) is digested by the mercury.
Silver, copper, iron,
tin, lead, and brass --
And bronze -- these seven metals,
having been anointed with the mercury and filtered,
become gold of fifteen <s>varṇa</s> (purity grade) --
this is gold, without doubt.

body.text: iha kūpavahmoṣṭabandhaḥ kāñcikahastamāno garte sudhāyāś chohayā lipto yadi vāguḍaṃ sahitena cūrṇena liptaḥ śuṣkaḥ san || 1
body.translated_text: Here, the construction of the furnace-mouth: in a pit the size of a hand's span in sour gruel, plastered with the coating of lime, or if plastered with powder combined with <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery), when dried -- ||1
This apparatus is called <s>bhūdhara</s> (earth-holder). ||2

body.text: tataḥ kācaliptamṛttikākāṃsyaṃ śarāve jīrṇe hemarājiṃ sūtaṃ tathāṣoḍaśabhāgena śuddhagandhakacūrṇaṃ vā kṣiptvopari mukhakācaliptamṛttikākoḍīyakaṃ dattvā karpaṭamṛttikayā liptvā taṃ śarāvaṃ sampuṭaṃ bhūdharayantramadhye muktvā haṭhāgnirjvālanīyaḥ || 3
body.translated_text: Then, having placed in a glass-clay-coated bronze dish the <s>hemarāji</s>-digested mercury together with a one-sixteenth part of purified <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) powder, placing on top a mouth-cover of glass-clay-coated <s>koḍīyaka</s> (small cup), sealing with cloth and clay, placing that sealed dish-pair into the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus -- a strong fire should be kindled. ||3
And the nature of purified <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) should be learned from the teacher's mouth. ||4

body.text: yataḥ sarvasminn apyatra granthe 'nyatrāpi ca śuddhagandhaka eva kīcanasi dvimūlabījam || 5
body.translated_text: For in this entire treatise and elsewhere too, purified <s>gandhaka</s> alone is the essential seed of two roots. ||5

body.text: ata eva sarvatra gandhakaśuddhiyuktir gopitaiṣeti jñeyam || 6
body.translated_text: Hence, everywhere the method of <s>gandhaka</s> purification is kept secret -- this should be understood. ||6

body.text: sadoṣe ca gandhake jārite na kāryasiddhiriti tu gurumukhād gandhakaśuddhir avagantavyā || 7
body.translated_text: And if <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) with defects is digested, the desired result is not achieved -- therefore the purification of <s>gandhaka</s> must be learned from the teacher's mouth. ||7

body.text: tathā pūrvakṣiptagandhakaṣoḍaśabhāge jīrṇe punaḥ koḍīyakamūrchāyāśugandhakaṣoḍaśabhāgaṃ kṣiptvā koḍīyakaṃ dattvā haṭhāgnir jvālanīyaḥ || 8
body.translated_text: Then, when the previously added one-sixteenth part of <s>gandhaka</s> is digested, again, having added a one-sixteenth part of purified <s>gandhaka</s> into the <s>koḍīyaka</s> (sublimation cup), placing the <s>koḍīyaka</s>, a strong fire should be kindled. ||8

body.text: evaṃ ca rasāt ṣaḍguṇaśuddhagandhake jīrṇe 'tīvaraktaḥ pārado bhavati || 9
body.translated_text: Thus, when six times the mercury's [weight] of purified <s>gandhaka</s> has been digested, the mercury becomes extremely red. ||9

body.text: tena ca rasena rūpyaṃ tāmraṃ lohaṃ vaṅgaṃ nāgaṃ pittalaṃ kāṃsyaṃ ceti sapta lohāni abhyañjya gālitāni pañcadaśasuvarṇāni bhavanti || 10
body.translated_text: And with that mercury, having anointed silver, copper, iron, tin, lead, brass, and bronze -- these seven metals -- and having filtered them, they become [gold of] fifteen <s>varṇa</s> (purity grade). ||10
Thus the fifth [procedure] is the <s>gandhaka</s>-digestion of mercury that has digested <s>hemarāji</s>. ||11

children.translated_text: <s>Khaṭikā</s> (chalk) [1], salt [2], <s>tūrī</s>
(touchstone) [2], <s>gairika</s> (ochre) mineral [4], <s>jīkaka</s> [5] --
For the purification-testing of gold,
these should be the five earths.
Having placed in the <s>bhūdhara</s> (earth-holder) apparatus
the mercury that has digested <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur),
adding the essence of <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar),
one-thirty-second part relative to the mercury,
At the mouth, a <s>koḍīyaka</s> should be placed
face-down as a lid.
It should be sealed with cloth and clay,
and then a strong fire should be kindled.
As each [portion] is digested, one should add repeatedly
the [one-thirty-second] part -- the mercury-purifier.
This should be digested equal to the mercury's [weight],
neither less nor more.
When the essence of <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) has been digested,
I shall describe the five earths:
<s>dādhīcheda</s> [2], <s>kaṣā</s> [3], <s>vartta</s> [4] --
for purification, the gold is purified.

body.translated_text: Here, <s>khaṭikā</s> (chalk) ||1
Salt ||2
<s>Tūrī</s> (touchstone) ||3

body.text: gairikavarṇikājīkaka ityetābhiḥ pañcabhir mṛttikābhiḥ parīkṣakāḥ kanakaṃ parīkṣyaṃ tena yathā || 4
body.translated_text: <s>Gairika</s> (ochre), <s>varṇikā</s> (coloring agent), and <s>jīkaka</s> -- with these five earths, the assayers test gold, in the following manner: ||4

body.text: kanakapattrāṇi kāñjikena kledayitvā rajakatyaktatūrīśuṣkalagadakaṃ lavaṇena samabhogena cūrṇayitvā karparaḥ paricūrṇas tadupari pattraṃ punaścūrṇaṃ punaḥ pattramevaṃ pattrāṇy uparyupari muktvopari punaḥ karparaṃ dattvā cūrṇena sarvataḥ pārśve vācchādya yāvadbhiḥ karparapuṭa ācchādyate tāvanti chagaṇakāni khaḍakitvāgni dattvā mucyate yadi ca jvalitvā svayaṃ tiṣṭhati || 5
body.translated_text: Having moistened gold leaves with sour gruel, powdering dried <s>tūrī</s> (touchstone) applied with washerman's [materials] and salt in equal proportions, spreading the powder in the cup, then a leaf on top, again powder, again a leaf -- thus placing leaves one upon another with the cup [covered by powder] on top, covering the sides completely with powder, as many cow-dung cakes as cover the cup-crucible should be arranged, fire applied, and left -- if it burns and then stops by itself, ||5

body.text: tadā punar dvitīyavāraṃ chagaṇakhaṇḍakapūrṇaḥ puṭo deyaḥ || 6
body.translated_text: Then a second round of crucible-firing full of cow-dung pieces should be given. ||6

body.text: evaṃ yadi malādhikyaṃ tadā tṛtīyo deyaḥ || 7
body.translated_text: Thus, if there is excess of impurity, a third [round] should be given. ||7

body.text: evaṃ citrakṣaṭakhaṭikayāpi golakakhaṭikayā vā lavaṇamiśrayāpi puṭadvayatrayadānena tadeva kāryam || 8
body.translated_text: Similarly, with <s>citraka-kṣaṭa-khaṭikā</s> or ball-chalk, mixed with salt too, by giving two or three crucible-firings, the same result [is achieved]. ||8
Now, if it is known [to still be impure] -- ||9

body.text: eva kṛte'pi sarvathā na śuddhaṃ dravyaṃ yadi vāvadūlotādikudhātumasādhikyaṃ tadāmasavāravarṇikayā jīkakeṇa vā lavaṇamiśreṇa pūrvarītyaiva puṭadvayatrayadāne sarvamalaśuddhiḥ || 10
body.translated_text: Even after doing thus, if the substance is in no way purified, or if there is excess of base metal impurity like <s>avadūla</s> etc., then with <s>amasa-vāra-varṇikā</s> or with <s>jīkaka</s> mixed with salt, by giving two or three crucible-firings in the same manner as before, all impurities are purified. ||10
Thus, purification of all defects by means of the five earths. ||11

body.text: tathā caturdaśavarṇikādaśīkādaśayanavāś ceti sampratikale svarṇaparamasīmā ataḥ paraṃ śodhane 'pi kṛte na hi karṇikāvṛddhiḥ || 12
body.translated_text: Similarly, the fourteen-<s>varṇikā</s> assay represents the present-day maximum limit of gold; beyond this, even if purification is done, there is no increase in <s>karṇikā</s> (touchstone test value). || 12

body.text: tathā śodhanacūrṇaṃ yadi dhmāyate tadā yo rūpyādidhātuś cīrṇo bhavati so 'pi labhyate || 13
body.translated_text: Similarly, if the purification powder is smelted, then whatever silver or other metal has been dissolved can also be recovered. || 13

body.text: tathā rūpyaṃ karpare kṣiptvoparisīsakaṃ kṣipyate'dho jālyate tato dvāv api sarāvedākatrabhūtvābhramatastadāvasīsakarajatamalaṃ caritvā karparalagitāgaraṇarakṣāṅgulapramāṇaś caramadhye milati || 14
body.translated_text: Similarly, when silver is placed in a cupel (<s>karpara</s>) and lead (<s>sīsaka</s>) is placed on top, and fire is applied below, then both become mixed with lead (<s>sarāvedāka</s>), and from that, the lead-silver impurity is consumed, and what remains in the cupel after settling is of the thickness of a finger of protection-ash (<s>rakṣā</s>). || 14

body.text: śuddharūpyarasaśca yadi bhrāntas tiṣṭhati tadā jñeyaṃ śuddho rūpyarasaḥ || 15
body.translated_text: If the pure silver-mercury, when rotated, remains spinning, then it should be known that the silver-mercury is pure. || 15
When the protection-ash is examined, the metals that were dissolved are recovered. || 16
Such matters should be understood from the mouths of the knowledgeable. || 17
Now, the commentary on the root text: || 18

body.text: bhūdharayantre śarāvasampuṭe jīrṇaṃ gandhakaṃ rasaṃ kṣiptvā dvātriṃśattamena manaḥśilāsattvaṃ ca kṣiptvā mukhe koḍīyakaṃ dattvā karpaṭamṛttikayā ca liptvā haṭhāgniṃ jvālayet jīrṇe ca manaḥśilāsattve punardvātriṃśattamena bhāgena tasya kṣepaḥ || 19
body.translated_text: In the <s>bhūdharayantra</s> (mountain apparatus), placing sulphur-absorbed mercury in a covered dish (<s>śarāvasampuṭa</s>), and adding the essence of <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) in the thirty-second part, placing a stopper (<s>koḍīyaka</s>) at the mouth, sealing with cloth-and-clay, one should kindle strong fire; and when the <s>manaḥśilā</s> essence is absorbed, the same should be added again in the thirty-second part. || 19

body.text: evaṃ punaḥ punaḥ kṣepaṇasūtatulyaṃ manaḥśilāsattvaṃ jāryam || 20
body.translated_text: Thus, by repeated addition, <s>manaḥśilā</s> essence equal to the mercury should be absorbed. || 20
Neither less nor more. || 21

body.text: evaṃ manaḥśilāsattve jīrṇe pāradena saptalohānyabhyaṅgagālitāni hemarūpāṇi bhavanti || 22
body.translated_text: When the <s>manaḥśilā</s> essence is thus absorbed, the mercury transmutes the seven metals, when smeared and filtered, into the form of gold. || 22

body.text: tacca hema pañcabhir mṛttikābhiḥ śodhanikāṃ sahate || 23
body.translated_text: And that gold withstands the purification test (<s>śodhanikā</s>) of five earths (clays). || 23
And it becomes pure through the tests of cutting (<s>cheda</s>), assay (<s>kaṣā</s>), and turning (<s>vartta</s>) purification. || 24
Thus the sixth process: the absorption (<s>jāraṇa</s>) of <s>manaḥśilā</s> essence into sulphur-absorbed mercury. || 25

body.text: etāvadbhiḥ saṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛto raso lohasādhaka eva || 26
body.translated_text: Mercury refined by this many <s>saṃskāras</s> is capable of transmuting metals (<s>lohasādhaka</s>) alone. || 26

body.text: ataḥ paraṃ ca ye saṃskārā yāni ca jāraṇāni tāni dehalohasādhakānīti || 27
body.translated_text: Beyond this, whatever further <s>saṃskāras</s> and absorptions (<s>jāraṇas</s>) there are, those are for transmuting the body and metals (<s>dehalohasādhaka</s>). || 27
Therein, the seventh — the absorption of <s>khāpara</s> (mica) essence — is stated: || 28

children.translated_text: The mercury with absorbed <s>śilā</s> (realgar) essence,
placed in a four-legged iron mortar,
with the powder of <s>khāpara</s> (mica) essence
in the sixty-fourth part,
grinding with <s>thūthāviḍa</s> (blue vitriol flux),
one should kindle gentle fire below;
as each portion is absorbed, adding more repeatedly,
eight times the mercury should be absorbed.
When the <s>puṣpākṣa</s> (mica) essence is absorbed,
the mercury becomes unctuous (<s>sasneha</s>);
it absorbs via the food-pathway (<s>annapatha</s>) and the mouth;
now the mercury rises upward.

body.text: catuṣpāde lohaṣairaleṣāparasūtvaṃ tasmāccatuḥṣaṣṭiguṇaṃ jīrṇamanaḥśilāsattvaṃ pāradaṃ ca kṣiptvā thūthāviḍena saṃpiṣann adho mṛduvahnir jvālayet || 1
body.translated_text: In the four-legged iron mortar, placing the <s>khāpara</s> (mica) essence in the sixty-fourth part, along with the mercury that has absorbed <s>manaḥśilā</s> essence, grinding with <s>thūthāviḍa</s> (blue vitriol flux), one should kindle gentle fire beneath the mortar. || 1

body.text: atratane ca khāparasattve jīrṇe punaḥ 64 bhāgena tadeva kṣepyam || 2
body.translated_text: And when the initial <s>khāpara</s> essence is absorbed, the same should be added again in the sixty-fourth part. || 2

body.text: evaṃ punaḥ punaḥ kṣiptvā rasādaṣṭaguṇaṃ khāparasattvaṃ jāraṇīyam || 3
body.translated_text: Thus, by repeated addition, <s>khāpara</s> essence eight times the mercury should be absorbed. || 3

body.text: tataḥ pāradaḥ sasneho vā saṃgratyūrdhvam annapathahīrakaṃ jīryati || 4
body.translated_text: Then the mercury becomes unctuous and, rising upward, absorbs diamond (<s>hīraka</s>) via the food-pathway (<s>annapatha</s>). || 4
Thus the seventh process: the absorption of <s>khāpara</s> essence into the mercury that had absorbed <s>śilā</s> essence. || 5
