children.translated_text: Of the three kinds of food-pathway (<s>annapatha</s>) diamonds (<s>vakra</s>),
one diamond from the middle;
the mercury by which the essence
born of <s>puṣpākṣa</s> (mica) has been absorbed,
placing both into the metal (iron) mortar,
the four-legged one,
grinding with <s>thūthāviḍa</s> (blue vitriol flux),
one should kindle gentle fire below.
Fire should be maintained for as long as
that diamond is absorbed;
when the diamond is absorbed via the food-pathway,
the mercury becomes all-pervading (<s>sarvavyāpī</s>).

body.translated_text: Later, the preparation of food-pathway diamonds of three kinds will be described. || 1

body.text: tatas teṣāṃ prakāratrayāṇāṃ madhyātprathamamekatamena prakāreṇa niṣpannam annapathe hīrakabhasma tathā jīrṇakhāparasattvaṃ sutaṃ cobhāv api catuṣpāde lohakhalve kṣiptvā thūthāviḍena piṣan kharalādho bhāge komalāgniṃ jvālayet || 2
body.translated_text: Then, the diamond-ash prepared by one method from among those three kinds, together with the mercury that has absorbed <s>khāpara</s> essence — both are placed in the four-legged iron mortar, and while grinding with <s>thūthāviḍa</s> (blue vitriol flux), gentle fire should be kindled below the mortar. || 2
This continues until all the diamond-ash is absorbed. || 3

body.text: tato hīrake jīrṇe sati rasaḥ sarvavyāpīti dehalohavyāpako bhavati || 4
body.translated_text: Then, when the diamond is absorbed, the mercury becomes all-pervading (<s>sarvavyāpī</s>) — that is, it becomes capable of pervading the body and metals (<s>dehaloha</s>). || 4
Thus the eighth process: the absorption of food-pathway diamond into the mercury that has absorbed <s>khāpara</s> essence. || 5

children.translated_text: Mercury that has become thus
acts as a fierce destroyer like <s>Rudra</s>;
whatever is given to it —
mercury, sub-metals (<s>uparasa</s>), or minerals (<s>vātaka</s>),
it devours all swiftly,
just as Lord <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord);
whatever falls into its mouth
is absorbed in an instant.
Gems up to and including crystal (<s>sphāṭika</s>)
are absorbed with great rapidity;
then, when ten million times its weight is absorbed,
the mercury becomes a <s>śaṅkhavedhī</s> (conch-piercer, i.e., supreme transmuter).
It instantly bestows immortality (<s>amaratva</s>)
and the power of flying through the sky (<s>khecaratva</s>);
if one who has not achieved absorption administers unprocessed
<s>tumbā</s>-seed mercury,
he is a slayer of <s>Brahman</s>, a wicked person,
and an enemy of mine, O <s>Maheśvarī</s>!
Therefore, with every effort,
one should kill (fix) the mercury after absorption;
placing cow dung on the ground,
then a crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>) upon it,
in the middle of that, adding oil
derived from <s>kaṭutumbī</s> (bitter gourd), one should place the mercury;
the juice of <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade) should be added,
equal to the oil, then again,
adding sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>) in the measure of a rice grain
and sealing it;
placing a cover (<s>śrāvaka</s>) on its back,
the physician should fill it to the brim.
Knowing it has cooled on its own,
that the oil and sulphur are absorbed,
one should add <s>kākamācī</s> juice and fire
again and again, causing absorption.
Placing moist cow dung
in the crucible and fire below,
sulphur six times the mercury should be absorbed;
thus the mercury becomes <s>muṣa</s> (crucible-worthy).
That mercury should be ground in the mortar
with lemon (<s>jambīra</s>) juice for a day;
first in the sixty-fourth part,
then in the thirty-second part,
then in the sixteenth part — pure gold
leaf should be absorbed into the mercury;
at each stage, it should be ground well
with lemon juice firmly.
<s>Mūlikā</s> (root-paste), salt, and sulphur —
in the absence of bile and oil,
ground with lemon juice,
the gold leaf should be coated with it.
Thus the absorption (<s>jāraṇā</s>) should be performed;
then the mercury should be killed (fixed).
Or else, this mercury without <s>muṣa</s> (crucible)
should be absorbed with the <s>viḍa</s> (flux) method;
I shall now describe the <s>viḍa</s> (flux) —
the best physician should prepare it.
Conch shell powder (<s>śaṅkhacūrṇa</s>) with <s>Arka</s> (milkweed) milk
should be soaked in sunlight for a day;
likewise with lemon juice,
for one day — <s>dhūmasāraka</s> (smoke-salt),
<s>sauvarcala</s> (black salt) with goat's urine —
decoction for four <s>yāmas</s> (watches);
<s>kaṇṭakārī</s> (thorny nightshade) juice decoction
for one day in human urine;
<s>sājīkṣāra</s> (borax) and <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol),
<s>tintiṇīka</s> (tamarind) and <s>śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch) —
soaked with lemon juice,
each for four <s>yāmas</s> (watches) separately;
<s>jepāla</s> (croton) seed with bark removed,
with radish juice for a day;
<s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), <s>guñjā</s> (rosary pea)
with <s>Śigru</s> root juice for a day;
all of this in equal parts
should be ground with lemon juice;
that ball should be carefully preserved —
this <s>viḍa</s> (flux) is called <s>vaḍabānala</s> (submarine fire).
By grinding mercury with this,
in a heated mortar, it devours
gold, mica, and all metals —
it absorbs essences (<s>sattvas</s>) in an instant.

body.translated_text: Now, <s>viḍas</s> (fluxes) according to other opinions: || 1
Now he describes the method for knowing whether substances to be absorbed have been absorbed or not: || 2

children.translated_text: The first is <s>garbha</s> (womb/embryonic), the next is <s>piṇḍa</s> (mass),
the third is <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation);
for all substances to be absorbed into mercury,
the absorption process is thus threefold.
When the substance has been absorbed into the mercury
and the mercury is filtered through cloth,
if everything remains in the cloth,
the first stage is called <s>garbha</s> (embryonic).
When the substance that was further absorbed
passes completely through the cloth,
and the mercury is slightly more in weight,
this upper stage is called <s>piṇḍa</s> (mass).
When the mercury, having been made to produce a net-like pattern,
passes through the cloth again,
and settles in its own fluid state,
the third stage is absorption complete (<s>jīrṇajārya</s>).

body.translated_text: Here too is the traditional procedure: || 1

body.text: ihānantaraproktaṃ dhānyābhrakādīnām [..] sa ca [..] tameṣv anyeṣu vastuṣu rase jāriteṣu sasūtakaṃ jīrṇam ajīrṇam eveti vicāraḥ || 2
body.translated_text: The previously stated mica (<s>dhānyābhra</s>) and other substances [...] and that [...] when these and other substances are absorbed into mercury, the consideration is whether it is absorbed or not yet absorbed with the mercury. || 2

body.text: prathamo garbhaḥ dvitīyaḥ piṇḍastṛtīyaḥ pariṇāmaka iti trividhaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ bhavati || 3
body.translated_text: The first is <s>garbha</s> (embryonic), the second is <s>piṇḍa</s> (mass), the third is <s>pariṇāmaka</s> (transformed) — thus the characteristics are threefold. || 3

body.text: tadyathā jāryaṃ vastu jārayitvā raso vastreṇa gālyate tato yadi kiṃcidvastre śeṣaṃ vigālya tiṣṭhati tadā jñeyo'sau garbha iti || 4
body.translated_text: That is: after absorbing the substance to be absorbed, the mercury is filtered through cloth; if something remains in the cloth without filtering through, then it should be known as <s>garbha</s> (embryonic). || 4

body.text: tataḥ punarapi saraś carubhyate tadeva kharale kṣiptvā yathā viḍena peṣitāgnirjvālanīyaḥ || 5
body.translated_text: Then, the mercury is taken again, placed in the mortar, and as before, fire should be kindled while grinding with <s>viḍa</s> (flux). || 5

body.text: ayaṃ bhāvo jāraṇā yena vidhinā pūrvaṃ bhaṇitāsti sā tena vidhinā jāryauṣadhaṃ vinaivānumānena taptvā punarvastreṇa raso gālanīyaḥ || 6
body.translated_text: The meaning is: the absorption procedure as previously described — by that same procedure, without adding fresh absorption medicine, heating by estimation alone, the mercury should again be filtered through cloth. || 6

body.text: tato yadi vastrātpūrvo 'pi niḥsarati nanu kiṃcil lagati paraṃ tolitaḥ sa tu nijataulyādhiko bhavati tadā jñeyo'sau piṇḍa iti || 7
body.translated_text: Then, if it passes through the cloth as before, but something still adheres slightly, and when weighed it is found to exceed its original weight, then it should be known as <s>piṇḍa</s> (mass). || 7
The meaning is: the medicine is still not fully absorbed. || 8

body.text: tataḥ punarapi yathā bhaṇitāsti tathaiva jāryauṣadhopakṣepeṇa vinaiva vidhāpunar navavastreṇa raso gālyate || 9
body.translated_text: Then again, in the same way as described, without adding fresh absorption medicine, by the procedure alone, the mercury is filtered through new cloth. || 9

body.text: yadi vastrānniḥsṛto gālitaḥ sannijataulye tiṣṭhati tadā jñeyo'sau pariṇāmaka iti || 10
body.translated_text: If, having passed through the cloth and been filtered, it remains at its original weight, then it should be known as <s>pariṇāmaka</s> (transformed). || 10

children.translated_text: * The meaning is: the medicine is completely absorbed by the mercury in every way.

children.text: * atrādyam etad dvayameva śuddhakṛto yo bhedaḥ śuddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: * Here, this first pair alone constitutes the pure distinction of purification.

body.translated_text: Thus the chapter on the characteristics of absorption of substances to be absorbed. || 12
Thus the section on <s>sāraṇa</s> (extraction) is concluded. || 13
Thus, with eight <s>saṃskāras</s>, the eleventh <s>saṃskāra</s> of absorption (<s>jāraṇā</s>) is complete. || 14

children.translated_text: Having made a hole at the bottom of a pot,
one should insert a cord with two knots,
one in the middle and one outside;
in the pot, a dripping timer (<s>galadghaṭī</s>) should be fashioned.
With a decoction of <s>mahoḍāka</s> (castor) roots
and sandalwood (<s>śrīkhaṇḍa</s>) in the pot,
placing in the middle of an iron dish (<s>ayaḥsthālikā</s>)
the mercury that has absorbed diamond,
placing a perforated lid (<s>ḍhaṅkaṇī</s>),
and the pot filled with sandalwood decoction
inverted upon the perforated lid,
one should kindle strong fire.
Below the iron dish for four watches (<s>yāmas</s>) —
through the hole in the lid,
the sandalwood extract (<s>śrīpiṇḍa</s>), dripping from the cord,
falls repeatedly upon the mercury.
That mercury, burnt and mixed with the drippings,
becomes white ash;
that should be placed in a blind crucible (<s>andhamūṣā</s>)
together with honey, ghee, and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>).
When smelted, it certainly achieves fixation (<s>bandha</s>)
of the mercury — there is no doubt;
it does not diminish even when smelted repeatedly,
having attained supreme stability.
And the mercury that, while being absorbed,
binds itself spontaneously —
that is indeed among the perfected mercuries (<s>siddharasa</s>);
it binds the metals of the body (<s>dehaloha</s>).

body.text: iha kumbhasya tale chidram aṅgulipraveśayogyaṃ kṛtvā tatra davarakaṃ kṣiptvā madhye bahirapi ca davarake granthiṃ dattvā tathā kāryaṃ yathā satkumbho galadghaṭī bhavati || 1
body.translated_text: Here, having made a hole in the bottom of the pot suitable for inserting a finger, placing a cord there, tying a knot in the middle and outside on the cord, it should be arranged such that the full pot becomes a dripping timer (<s>galadghaṭī</s>). || 1
The meaning is: the medicinal liquid placed therein drips through. || 2

body.text: tataḥ sthālikāmadhye jīrṇadorakaṃ pāradaṃ kṣiptvā upari sacchidrā pradhvarā ḍhaṅkaṇī dīyate || 3
body.translated_text: Then, placing the diamond-absorbed mercury in the iron dish, a perforated inverted lid (<s>ḍhaṅkaṇī</s>) is placed on top. || 3

body.text: tasyāścopari galadghaṭī kumbhomumutkā mahoḍākamūlānāṃ śrīṣaṇḍena sakumbho bhriyate || 4
body.translated_text: Upon that, the dripping-timer pot is placed mouth-down, and the pot is filled with the decoction of <s>mahoḍāka</s> roots and sandalwood. || 4

body.text: tataḥ sthālikāyā adhastāc caturo yāmān haṭhāgnir jvālanīyaḥ || 5
body.translated_text: Then, strong fire (<s>haṭhāgni</s>) should be kindled below the iron dish for four watches. || 5

body.text: evaṃ ca yathā yathā kumbhamadhyāḍḍhaṅkaṇī chidreṇa davarakād galitvā tuṣarasaḥ pārade patati tathā tathāgnidagdhaḥ pāradaḥ śvetabhasma bhavati || 6
body.translated_text: Thus, as the husk-liquid drips from the cord through the hole in the lid from within the pot onto the mercury, the mercury burned by fire becomes white ash. || 6

body.text: tataśca tatsūtabhasma madhvājyaṭaṅkaṇaiḥ sākaṃ bandhamūṣāyāṃ kṣiptvā dhmāyate || 7
body.translated_text: Then, that mercury-ash, together with honey, ghee, and borax, is placed in a binding crucible (<s>bandhamūṣā</s>) and smelted. || 7
Then the mercury, when smelted, becomes fixed (<s>baddha</s>). || 8

body.text: ko 'rthaḥ anekaśo 'tyarthaṃ dhmāto'pi niścalo bhavati na punaḥ kṣīyate || 9
body.translated_text: What is the meaning? Even when smelted repeatedly and intensely, it becomes stable and does not diminish further. || 9

body.text: yaḥ pārado jāryamāṇaḥ san badhyate svayameva nibadhyate nirāyāsabaddho bhavati sa hi siddharasa ityucyate || 10
body.translated_text: The mercury which, while being absorbed, binds itself spontaneously — becomes bound effortlessly — that is called <s>siddharasa</s> (perfected mercury). || 10
And that becomes capable of piercing (<s>vedhaka</s>) the body and metals. || 11
Thus, by the method previously described, that <s>siddharasa</s> (perfected mercury) is accomplished. || 12
Now he describes the fruits (results) of <s>siddharasa</s>: || 13

children.translated_text: In the not-fully-dark eyes of a deer,
and in a blind person's eyes that sprout sight,
when anointed with that mercury — in both cases, the affliction
the blind one is destroyed and the blind one sees.
By <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>dānavas</s> (demons), <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians),
<s>siddhas</s> (perfected beings), <s>guhyakas</s> (hidden beings), and sky-travelers,
he in whose mouth the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) is placed —
his movement in the sky is not destroyed.
He does not die even by poison,
nor is he burned by fire.
In the sky, the one who possesses the <s>siddhavidyā</s> (perfected knowledge),
though dead, revives at that very instant.
Even compared to gems, <s>mantras</s>, and herbs,
the superior power is great.
The one named '<s>mṛtasaṃjīvana</s>' (reviver of the dead) —
this <s>rasabandha</s> (mercury fixation) is proclaimed.

body.translated_text: When the eyes of a deer are anointed with prepared <s>rasa</s> (mercury), ||1
the affliction of the eyes is destroyed. ||2
When <s>siddharasa</s> (perfected mercury) collyrium is applied to blind eyes, the blind one sees. ||3

body.text: tathā yasya mukhe siddharasaguṭikā tiṣṭhati tasyākāśe gatir devadānavagandharvasiddhayakṣakhecarair na hanyate || 4
body.translated_text: Likewise, he in whose mouth a <s>siddharasa</s> (perfected mercury) pill remains — his movement in the sky is not destroyed by <s>devas</s>, <s>dānavas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>siddhas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and sky-travelers. ||4

body.text: tathā siddharase mukhe sthite viṣeṇa na mriyate || 5
body.translated_text: Likewise, with <s>siddharasa</s> placed in the mouth, one does not die by poison. ||5
One is not burned by fire. ||6
In the sky, one attains <s>siddharasavidyā</s> (the knowledge of perfected mercury). ||7
Being dead — that is, having fainted — one revives at that very instant. ||8
Likewise, even compared to gems, <s>mantras</s>, and great herbs, the superior power of <s>siddharasa</s> is greater. ||9
This <s>rasabandha</s> (mercury fixation) named '<s>mṛtajīvana</s>' (reviver of the dead) is described. ||10
What is the meaning of '<s>mṛta</s>' (dead)? One who is dead as if dead. ||11

body.text: sarpadaṃśavahnidāhajalaplāvaśastraghātaviṣādiduṣṭaprayogair mūrchitaḥ yaḥ kenāpi jīvayituṃ na śakyate so 'pi mukhe kṣiptasyāsya rasasya prabhāveṇa kṣaṇād eva jīvati || 12
body.translated_text: One who has fainted from snake-bite, fire-burn, flood, weapon-strike, poison, and other harmful applications, whom no one is able to revive — even such a one, by the power of this <s>rasa</s> placed in the mouth, revives in an instant. ||12
Thus the twelfth <s>saṃskāra</s> (processing), the <s>bandha</s> (fixation) of aged diamond-mercury. ||13

children.translated_text: Sixty-four <s>palas</s> of fixed mercury
the wise one should melt down;
sixty-four <s>palas</s> of gold-streak
should be melted separately.
That gold-streak should be poured
upon the melted fixed mercury;
thus a red <s>ṣoṭa</s> (alloy) is produced —
this <s>saṃskāra</s> is known as <s>sāraṇa</s> (extraction).

body.text: pūrvoktayuktyā baddhasūtasya catuḥṣaṣṭipalāni gālayitvā tato dvitīyamuṣāyāṃ hemarājicatuḥṣaṣṭipalāni gālayet || 1
body.translated_text: By the method stated before, sixty-four <s>palas</s> of fixed mercury should be melted; then, in a second crucible, sixty-four <s>palas</s> of gold-streak should be melted. ||1
Then those sixty-four <s>palas</s> of gold-streak should be poured upon the sixty-four <s>palas</s> of melted fixed mercury. ||2
Then, when both are combined, a red <s>ṣoṭa</s> (alloy) is produced. ||3
Thus this <s>sāraṇa</s> (extraction) <s>saṃskāra</s> is described. ||4
Thus the thirteenth <s>saṃskāra</s>, the <s>sāraṇa</s> (extraction) of fixed mercury. ||5

children.translated_text: Having placed [the mercury] inside silver,
one should precipitate the <s>rasa</s> as before,
ground together with gold paste,
triturated with <s>kumārī</s> (aloe vera) juice.
The bottom of the upper vessel
should be firmly smeared [with this].
Thus, with sulphur, copper,
silver, and gold likewise,
it should be precipitated again and again;
thus one should process it further.
However many <s>gadyāṇas</s> (weight units) of red <s>ṣoṭa</s>
are produced after <s>sāraṇa</s> (extraction),
double that of pure <s>śilā</s> (realgar)
should be thoroughly powdered repeatedly.
In a wide glass flask, that
powder should be placed above and below,
and the red <s>ṣoṭa</s> in the middle;
having placed it, and [adding] a <s>mica</s> lid,
seven layers of clay
should be given to the flask.
Having dug a pit the height of a man
and filled it with cow-dung cakes,
having placed the flask in the middle,
a strong fire should then be lit.
When it has cooled by itself, it should be collected —
this is called <s>māraṇa</s> (calcination).

body.text: iha sāraṇasaṃskāre kṛte yāvanto raktaṣoṭasya gadyāṇā bhavanti tebhyo dviguṇāttu śuddhamanaḥśilāgadyāṇān gāḍhaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇarūpān kṛtvā prauḍhakācakūpīmadhye 'rdhacūrṇaṃ kṣiptvā tato raktaṣoṭaṃ muktvā punarupari śeṣaṃ manaḥśilācūrṇam adhaḥ kṣiptvā kūpīmadhye'dhaścūrṇaṃ kṣiptvā tato raktaṣoṭaṃ muktvā punarupari śeṣaṃ manaḥśilācūrṇamadhaḥ liptvā kūpīdvāre 'bhrasya cātikāṃ dattvā saptatāraṃ tasyāṃ kūpikāyāṃ paritaḥ karpaṭamṛttikāṃ dattvāraṇyachāṇakaiḥ pūrṇāyāṃ puruṣapramāṇakhanitagartāyāṃ madhye kūpīṃ muktvā haṭhāgnir jvālanīyaḥ || 1
body.translated_text: Here, after the <s>sāraṇa</s> processing, however many <s>gadyāṇas</s> of red <s>ṣoṭa</s> there are, double the <s>gadyāṇas</s> of pure <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) should be made into a fine, dense powder. Having placed half the powder in the middle of a mature glass flask, then placing the red <s>ṣoṭa</s>, and again placing the remaining <s>manaḥśilā</s> powder above, having smeared below, having placed the powder below in the middle of the flask, then placing the red <s>ṣoṭa</s>, and again placing the remaining <s>manaḥśilā</s> powder below, having smeared, and having placed a mica cap at the flask's opening, applying cloth-and-clay seven times around that flask, in a pit dug to man-height filled with forest cow-dung cakes, the flask should be placed in the middle and a strong fire should be lit. ||1

body.text: yadi ca jvalitā svayaṃ śītalaṃ bhavati tadā kūpīmadhyāt sa raso grāhyaḥ || 2
body.translated_text: And when, having burned, it becomes cool by itself, then the <s>rasa</s> should be collected from the middle of the flask. ||2
This is called <s>māraṇa</s> (calcination). ||3
Here is the traditional instruction: ||4

body.text: khaḍḍāyām ardhaṃ yāvacchaṇakāni muktvopari kūpī mucyate tataḥ pārśveṣattathopari chāṇakair gartā bhriyate || 5
body.translated_text: In the pit, cow-dung cakes should be placed up to half, then the flask is placed on top; then the pit should be filled with cow-dung cakes on the sides and above. ||5
Thus the fourteenth <s>saṃskāra</s>, the <s>māraṇa</s> (calcination) of extracted mercury. ||6

children.translated_text: The mercury, processed through <s>Manu</s>-numbered [fourteen]
<s>saṃskāras</s> and calcined,
having been placed in a mortar and ground —
this is called <s>pratisāraṇa</s> (re-grinding).

body.text: iha manusaṃkhyaiś caturdaśabhiḥ saṃskārair anantaroktaiḥ saṃskṛtya yo māritasūtaḥ sukhalve kṣiptvātyarthaṃ piṣyate || 1
body.translated_text: Here, the mercury that has been calcined after being processed through the fourteen <s>saṃskāras</s> stated immediately before — having placed it in a fine mortar, it should be ground exceedingly. ||1
This is called <s>pratisāraṇa</s> (re-grinding). ||2
Thus the fifteenth <s>saṃskāra</s>, the <s>pratisāraṇa</s> of calcined mercury. ||3

children.translated_text: The calcined [mercury] with killed lead,
and gold — its powder too —
which is to be added during <s>pratisāraṇa</s> —
this is called <s>krāmaṇa</s> (transmutation).

body.text: iha mṛtasīsakena kāñcanaṃ sārayitvā tasya mṛtakāñcanasya cūrṇaṃ yat pratisāritarase kṣipyate || 1
body.translated_text: Here, having extracted gold with killed lead, the powder of that killed gold is what is added to the re-ground <s>rasa</s>. ||1
This is called <s>krāmaṇa</s> (transmutation). ||2
Thus the sixteenth <s>saṃskāra</s>, the <s>krāmaṇa</s> of re-ground mercury. ||3
The method of killing lead and gold will be stated by [the author] himself later. ||4

children.translated_text: With a leaf of the betel plant,
that [mercury]... (text uncertain)
one should add a <s>rati</s>-measure (a small unit) and make
a pellet of the lead-leaf.
Having melted, that powder
should be placed in all metals.
When the metals are being melted, it should be weighed —
one that penetrates a thousand [parts].

body.text: iha prathamaṃ śuddhanāgasyaikena patrevadyena patraṃ kṛtvā tatra ratimātraṃ kramitaṃ rasaṃ kṣiptvā nārāpatrasthātanugālayitvā veḍhanīṃ ca kṛtvā tāṃ veḍhanīṃ gālayet |
body.translated_text: Here, first, having made a leaf from one leaf-weight of pure lead, placing a <s>rati</s>-measure of transmuted <s>rasa</s> upon it, making a pellet from the lead-leaf and melting it,
then it becomes a powder.

body.text: tataḥ pūrvoktāni sarvāṇyapi nāgavaṅgādilohāni ratisahasramātrāṇi gālayitvā bhramatyeva loharase ratimātraṃ veḍhanīrasaṃ cūrṇaṃ kṣipet |
body.translated_text: Then, having melted all the aforementioned metals — lead, tin, and other metals — in the amount of a thousand <s>ratis</s>, one should add a <s>rati</s>-measure of the pellet-<s>rasa</s> powder to the molten metal.
Then the gold adhering to the bottom should be collected.

children.translated_text: * This is the <s>rasa</s> that penetrates a thousand [parts].
* Thus the seventeenth <s>saṃskāra</s>, the <s>vedhaka</s> (penetration) of transmuted mercury. ||
In a melted <s>gadyāṇa</s> of lead,
one should add a <s>gadyāṇa</s> of mercury;
in the middle of that powder should be added
a <s>gadyāṇa</s> of sulphur too.
And a <s>gadyāṇa</s> of <s>sarjikā</s> (borax)
combined — there would be a group of four.
Having ground into powder,
one should then mix with water.
Having placed in a sealed pair of dishes,
with hole-free cloth and clay,
having dug a hand-height pit
and filled it with cow-dung cakes,
having placed the sealed dish-pair in the pit,
one should then light the fire.
When it has cooled by itself, having taken it out,
it should be made into a fine powder.
Then, in the pierced mercury that has been melted,
having added a mustard-seed measure,
when thus done, the <s>udghāṭana</s> (opening / activation)
of the mercury certainly takes place.

body.translated_text: Then in the middle of that powder, a <s>gadyāṇa</s> of sulphur [should be placed]. ||1
And a <s>gadyāṇa</s> of <s>sarjikā</s> (borax) should be added. ||2

body.text: tato gālitanāgagadyāṇakaḥ 1 sūtagadyāṇakaḥ 2 gandhakagadyāṇakaḥ 1 evaṃ gadyāṇakacatuṣṭayaṃ melayitvā gāḍhaṃ sampiṣya cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā jalenāloḍayitvā punaḥ śoṣayitvā tataḥ śarāvasampuṭe kṣiptvā sampuṭasaṃdhau ca vastramṛttikāṃ dattvā tato hastapramāṇāyāṃ gartāyāṃ madhye chāṇakāni kṣiptvopari śarāvasampuṭaṃ dattvā muktvā punaḥ pārśveṣūpari chāṇakaiḥ khaṇḍībhūtvāgnir jvālanīyaḥ || 3
body.translated_text: Then, one <s>gadyāṇa</s> of melted lead, one <s>gadyāṇa</s> of mercury, one <s>gadyāṇa</s> of sulphur — thus combining a group of four <s>gadyāṇas</s>, grinding firmly, making into powder, mixing with water, drying again, then placing in a sealed pair of dishes, applying cloth-and-clay at the joint of the seal, then placing cow-dung cakes in the middle of a hand-height pit, placing the sealed dish-pair on top, then filling the sides and above with cow-dung cakes, the fire should be lit in portions. ||3

body.text: yadi ca jvalitvā na svayaṃ sthito bhavati tadā sampuṭamadhyād auṣadhaṃ gṛhītvā sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ kṛtvā vedhasaṃskṛtasya gālitasya rasasya madhye sarṣapamātraṃ gadyāṇacatuṣṭayaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ kṣipet || 4
body.translated_text: And when, having burned, it does not stand by itself [i.e., cools], then taking the medicine from within the sealed dishes, making it into a fine powder, in the middle of the melted <s>rasa</s> that has undergone the <s>vedha</s> processing, one should add a mustard-seed measure — a group of four <s>gadyāṇas</s> — of fine powder. ||4

body.text: atra ca sūtamadhye kṣepyauṣadhasya pramāṇaṃ bhaṇitam || 5
body.translated_text: And here the measure of the medicine to be added to the mercury is stated. ||5
But not [the measure] of the pierced mercury. ||6
Likewise, even by the masters, the measure of this has not been stated. ||7
Hence it is known by inference. ||8
Elsewhere, sixty-four <s>palas</s> of mercury are stated. ||9

body.text: tatastāvatā rasena yāvadauṣadhaṃ vedhasaṃskāre kriyamāṇe niṣpannaṃ tāvat evauṣadhasya rasasya madhye gadyāṇakacatuṣṭayaṃ pūrṇaṃ sarṣapamātraṃ kṣeptavyam || 10
body.translated_text: Therefore, with that much mercury, however much medicine is produced during the <s>vedha</s> processing, that full amount — a group of four <s>gadyāṇas</s> — should be added in a mustard-seed measure to the mercury. ||10
Truly, by the teacher's command, one knows the proper measure. ||11

body.text: evaṃ sarṣapamātre cūrṇe kṣipte viddhasūtasyodghāṭanaṃ bhavati || 12
body.translated_text: Thus, when the powder is added in a mustard-seed measure, the <s>udghāṭana</s> (activation) of the pierced mercury occurs. ||12
<s>Udghāṭana</s> (activation) means: [the capacity] for penetrating all metals and for removing all diseases. ||13
Thus the eighteenth <s>saṃskāra</s>. ||14

children.translated_text: One part of live copper,
two parts of pure gold,
melting together the three parts,
one should make a well-fused plate.
Having ground on a stone with lemon juices
that which has eaten the <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) [i.e., realgar processed with mercury],
a coating should be given with that
on both sides of the composite plate.
Six parts of <s>citrakūṭa</s> (chalk)
and one part of salt,
having powdered in equal proportion,
a crucible (<s>sthālikā</s>) should then be filled.
The coated plate should be placed in the middle
rolled up, with the opening upward.
With an inverted dish placed [on top],
the neck should be sealed with clay without holes.
Then, on top, one should place face-down
a <s>ḍhaṅkaṇī</s> (cover-dish) upon the dish.
Below the crucible, for four watches (twelve hours),
a strong fire should be lit underneath.
By this very method, indeed,
the plate becomes three layers.
Taking the middle layer,
one should discard the two side layers.
And from the powder of the middle layer,
<s>hemarāji</s> (gold-streak) is certainly produced.
By giving it in a sixty-fourth part,
the mercury should be dissolved eight-fold.

body.text: iha mānaśulbaṃ mārayitvā punar jīvyate taṃ jīvantaṃ śulvaṃ kathayanti || 1
body.translated_text: Here, copper is killed and then revived — they call that the 'living copper.' ||1

body.text: tatastacchulbasyaiko bhāgaḥ tathā dvau hemabhāgau evaṃ bhāgatrayaṃ gālayitvā iti tat sthūlaṃ pattraṃ kuryāt || 2
body.translated_text: Then, one part of that copper and two parts of gold — thus melting three parts together, a thick plate should be made. ||2

body.text: tato manaḥśilāyāṃ nimbukarasaiśca nāgaṃ mārayitvā jatupattram ubhayapārśvayos tena māritanāgena lepanīyam || 3
body.translated_text: Then, having killed lead with <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) and lemon juices, the composite plate should be coated on both sides with that killed lead. ||3

body.text: tataścitrakūṭakhaṭīlavaṇayoḥ samabhāgena cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā sthālīṃ bhṛtvā tasya madhye ūrdhvaṃ bruḍantaṃ pattraṃ muktvā mukhe'dhomukhaṃ śarāvaṃ kṛtvā sādha kaṇṭhe mṛdā liptvā śarāvasyoparyadhomukhaṃ ḍhaṅkaṇīṃ dattvā sthālikādhaḥ praharacatuṣkaṃ yāvat haṭhāgnir jvālanīyaḥ || 4
body.translated_text: Then, having made a powder of <s>citrakūṭa</s> chalk and salt in equal proportion, filling a crucible, placing the plate rolled up with opening upward in the middle, placing an inverted dish at the mouth, smearing the joint with clay, placing a <s>ḍhaṅkaṇī</s> face-down above the dish, below the crucible a strong fire should be lit for four watches. ||4

body.text: evaṃ ca kṛte pattrasya phāḍītrayaṃ jāyate || 5
body.translated_text: And when this is done, three layers of the plate are produced. ||5

body.text: tato yā madhyamā phāḍī tāṃ gṛhītvā mardanīyaṃ pārśvaphāḍīdvayam ca tyajanīyaṃ yacca madhyaphāḍīcūrṇaṃ sā hemarājir ucyate || 6
body.translated_text: Then, taking the middle layer and grinding it, the two side layers should be discarded; and the powder of the middle layer — that is called <s>hemarāji</s> (gold-streak). ||6

body.text: tasya catuḥṣaṣṭitamo bhāgaḥ pūrvoktayuktyā pūrvaproktasya rasasya dātavyaḥ || 7
body.translated_text: Its sixty-fourth part should be given to the mercury as described by the method stated before. ||7

body.text: evaṃ tāvadyāvadaṣṭaguṇo hemarājiṃ dattvā pūrvoktarītyā jāritā bhavati || 8
body.translated_text: Thus, as much as eight-fold <s>hemarāji</s> is given and dissolved by the method stated before. ||8
Thus the supreme <s>hemarāji</s> (gold-streak) [procedure] is complete. ||9

children.translated_text: <s>Nāgarāji</s> (lead-streak) is of ordinary [quality];
<s>mākṣikī</s> (pyrite-streak) is considered medium;
<s>ghoṣarāji</s> (brass-streak) is excellent;
that which is <s>prakāśa</s>-[streak] is the best of all.
One <s>pala</s> of <s>tīkṣṇaloha</s> (iron/steel),
two <s>palas</s> of bell-metal,
nine <s>palas</s> of copper,
three <s>palas</s> of brass,
fifteen <s>palas</s> (in <s>tithi</s>-number) of lead
killed with <s>śilā</s> (realgar),
and thirty <s>palas</s> — the wise one
should place in a crucible and melt.
Then gold-pyrite,
seven and a half <s>palas</s>,
adding little by little,
the wise one should melt slowly.
When it becomes equal
to the copper portion in amount,
a small amount of <s>prakāśarāji</s> (lustrous streak) results —
this is proclaimed as the first [grade].

body.text: iha yā nāgarājiḥ sā sāmānyā svalpakāryakārī || 1
body.translated_text: Here, <s>nāgarāji</s> (lead-streak) is of ordinary [quality], accomplishing minor tasks. ||1
<s>Mākṣikārāji</s> (pyrite-streak) accomplishes medium tasks. ||2
<s>Vyoṣarāji</s> (trikatu-streak) is excellent, accomplishing many tasks. ||3

body.text: ayaḥprakāśarājistābhyaḥ sarvābhyo rājibhya uttamā sarvottamakārīty arthaḥ || 4
body.translated_text: The <s>ayaḥprakāśa</s> (iron-lustre) <s>rāji</s> (streak/grade) is the best of all <s>rājis</s> — meaning it produces the most excellent results. ||4
Therefore, the <s>ayaḥprakāśa rāji</s> (iron-lustre grade) is described first. ||5
One <s>pala</s> (unit of weight) of <s>sāraloha</s> (steel),
two <s>palas</s> of <s>kāṃsya</s> (bell-metal), nine <s>palas</s> of purified <s>tāmra</s> (copper), three <s>palas</s> of <s>pittala</s> (brass),
fifteen <s>palas</s> of <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar)-killed <s>nāga</s> (lead). ||8
Thus, the total of all quantities being thirty <s>palas</s>, they should be placed in a crucible and smelted. ||9

body.text: tataḥ suvarṇamākṣikasya sārdhasaptapalānyānīya stokena madhye kṣiptvā punaḥ śanaistāvadāvartanīyāni yāvatā tāmrabhāgapramāṇāni bhavanti || 10
body.translated_text: Then, having brought seven and a half <s>palas</s> of <s>suvarṇamākṣika</s> (gold-pyrite), gradually adding it to the middle, it should again be slowly smelted until it becomes equal to the measure of the copper portion. ||10
This is the meaning: ||11
The copper [amounts to] nine <s>palas</s>. ||12

body.text: tataḥ sarvo rasa āvartayitvā yadā navapalapramāṇo bhavati tadā prathamāsāv ayaḥprakāśarājiḥ kathyate || 13
body.translated_text: Then, having smelted the entire preparation, when it becomes nine <s>palas</s> in quantity, it is then called the first <s>ayaḥprakāśa rāji</s> (iron-lustre grade). ||13
Thus the supreme <s>ayaḥprakāśa rāji</s> (iron-lustre grade) is described. ||14

children.translated_text: With powder of <s>tīkṣṇaloha</s> (sharp iron/steel)
and an equal amount of <s>kāṃsya</s> (bell-metal) powder,
having placed them in a crucible and smelted,
a single mass is made.
Half the quantity of the mass in <s>nāga</s> (lead)
should be added and digested again and again;
when the <s>nāga</s> is digested, the <s>vyoṣa rāji</s> (pungent-triad grade) results,
[with] <s>nāga</s> being six times the <s>kāṃsya</s>.

body.text: sāralohacūrṇaṃ kāṃsyacūrṇaṃ ca samamātrayā mūṣāyāṃ kṣiptvā tata āvartya ekapiṇḍaṃ kriyate || 1
body.translated_text: Having placed equal measures of <s>sāraloha</s> (steel) powder and <s>kāṃsya</s> (bell-metal) powder into a crucible, then smelting them, a single mass is made. ||1

body.text: tatastasmātpiṇḍād ardhamātrayā śuddhanāgaṃ madhye kṣiptvā mūṣāyāṃ punaḥ punarāvartya jāraṇīyam || 2
body.translated_text: Then, adding purified <s>nāga</s> (lead) in half the quantity of that mass into the middle of the crucible, it should be digested again and again. ||2
Then, again adding <s>nāga</s> in half-quantity, it should be digested. ||3

body.text: yadi caivaṃ punaḥ punarjāraṇena kāṃsyāt ṣaḍguṇaṃ nāgaṃ jīrṇaṃ bhavati || 4
body.translated_text: If thus, through repeated digestion, the <s>nāga</s> digested becomes six times the <s>kāṃsya</s>, ||4
then the <s>vyoṣa rāji</s> (pungent-triad grade) is produced. ||5
Thus the <s>vyoṣa rāji</s>, meaning the <s>kāṃsya rāji</s> (bell-metal grade). ||6

children.translated_text: Four <s>palas</s> of purified <s>tāmra</s> (copper)
should be smelted separately;
four <s>palas</s> of <s>thūthā</s> (blue vitriol),
and four <s>palas</s> of <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite).
The powder made from [the latter] eight <s>palas</s>
should be added little by little;
when only the copper remains,
it is considered the <s>mākṣika</s>-born <s>rāji</s> (pyrite grade).

body.text: prathamaṃ śuddhatāmrasya catvāri palāni pṛthag āvartayitvā tatastanmadhye thūthāpalāni catvāri catvāri mākṣīkapalānyevamaṣṭau palāni cūrṇīkṛtya stokena stokena kṣiptvā punaḥ punarāvartya tāvajjārayet || 1
body.translated_text: First, having smelted four <s>palas</s> of purified <s>tāmra</s> (copper) separately, then adding into its middle four <s>palas</s> of <s>thūthā</s> (blue vitriol) and four <s>palas</s> of <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) — thus eight <s>palas</s> powdered and added little by little — it should be smelted and digested repeatedly. ||1
Until only the copper remains. ||2
The meaning is that all the medicinal substance [totaling] four <s>palas</s> is digested. ||3
Thus the third, the <s>mākṣika rāji</s> (pyrite grade). ||4

children.translated_text: A portion of <s>śulva</s> (copper)
should be slowly smelted separately;
eight [parts] of <s>śilā</s> (realgar)-killed <s>nāga</s> (lead),
four parts of <s>thūthā</s> (blue vitriol).
Having ground [these] into powder, into the powdered <s>śulva</s> (copper)
one should add little by little;
this becomes the <s>nāga rāji</s> (lead grade)
The powder of metals elevated by the <s>rājis</s> (grades)
should always be made by the wise;
and from each, one <s>rāji</s> at a time
should be digested eightfold from mercury.

body.text: śuddhatāmrasya bhāgamekaṃ mūṣāyāṃ gālayitvā tato manaḥśilāyā bhāgāś catvāro mṛtanāgasya bhāgāstathā catvāraḥ tathā catvāraḥ thūthābhāgāḥ || 1
body.translated_text: Having melted one part of purified <s>tāmra</s> (copper) in a crucible, then four parts of <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar), likewise four parts of killed <s>nāga</s> (lead), and likewise four parts of <s>thūthā</s> (blue vitriol). ||1

body.text: evaṃ dvādaśabhāgāṃścūrṇīkṛtya stokena śulvamadhye kṣiptvā tāvadāvartayed yāvattāmraśeṣaṃ bhavati || 2
body.translated_text: Thus, having powdered the twelve parts and adding them little by little into the copper, it should be smelted until only the copper remains. ||2
This is called the <s>nāga rāji</s> (lead grade). ||3

body.text: thūthānāgarājīnāṃ phalamāha rājyabhyucchritalohānām ityādi catasṛṇāmapi rājīnāṃ lohasya cūrṇaṃ kṛtvaikaikarājiḥ || 4
body.translated_text: He states the result of the <s>thūthā</s>-<s>nāga rājis</s>: 'of the metals elevated by the <s>rājis</s>' etc. — having made a powder of the metal of each of the four <s>rājis</s>, one <s>rāji</s> at a time, ||4
should be digested eightfold into mercury using the mercury-preparation method described earlier, in sequence — thus is the procedure for making the <s>rājis</s>. ||5
Thus the fourth, the <s>nāga rāji</s> (lead grade). ||6
Now, the method for extracting the essence of <s>khāpara</s> (zinc calx):

children.translated_text: One <s>maṇa</s> (unit of weight) of <s>rasaka</s> (zinc ore / calamine),
boiled for three days
with human urine, then dried in the sun,
should be cooked for one <s>yāma</s> (watch, ~3 hours) with milk.
When dried and powdered, into that
an eighth part of <s>khala</s> (residue/oil-cake) should be added,
a quarter part of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa kṣāra</s> (borax),
and an eighth part of old <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery).
In two well-fired earthen crucibles
of round <s>kacūla</s> (bowl) shape,
the powder should be placed inside one,
and the crucible should be [sealed] around the powder.
Upon the other, a tube
fourteen <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-breadths) [tall],
made of clay, with a hole at the bottom,
should be placed — that one facing downward.
Sealing the entire [apparatus] all around
with cloth and clay,
the apparatus of the gourd-tube type
should be made for the essence-extraction.
The apparatus should be placed inside a furnace,
and with charcoal of <s>babbūla</s> (acacia) and <s>khadira</s> (catechu) trees
and similar [woods],
filling and filling, one should blow repeatedly.
And supporting with similar [instruments],
the downward-facing [crucible] through the middle of the tube —
until everything held within the crucible
has [descended as] the <s>khāpara</s> (zinc) essence.

body.text: rasakasya khāparasya maṇamekaṃ naramūtreṇa dinatrayaṃ kvāthayitvā ātape dattvā śoṣayitvā praharamekaṃ dugdhena pācayitvā punaḥ śoṣayitvā cūrṇīkṛtya tanmadhye'ṣṭabhāgena khalaścaturthabhāgena ṭaṅkaṇakṣāro'ṣṭamabhāgena pūrvaguḍa etāni trīṇi kṣipet || 1
body.translated_text: Having boiled one <s>maṇa</s> of <s>rasaka</s> (zinc ore/calamine, i.e., <s>khāpara</s>) in human urine for three days, drying it in the sun, cooking it for one <s>yāma</s> (watch) in milk, then drying and powdering it again — into that, one should add an eighth part of <s>khala</s> (oil-cake), a quarter part of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa kṣāra</s> (borax), and an eighth part of old <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) — these three. ||1

body.text: tato mṛttikayā mūṣādvayaṃ kaccolakasamānaṃ prauḍhaṃ vartulākāraṃ kṛtvā ekasyāṃ mūṣāyāṃ pūrvoktakhāparacūrṇaṃ kṣiptvā sā mūṣādhomukhī nālopari moktavyā || 2
body.translated_text: Then, making a pair of crucibles from clay — robust, round in shape like a <s>kaccola</s> (small bowl) — placing the <s>khāpara</s> powder described above in one crucible, that crucible should be released face-down upon the tube. ||2

body.text: tataḥ karpaṭamṛttikayā sarvapārśveṣu niśchidraṃ vidhāya sattvapātanāya īdṛśas tumbanalī nāmā yantraḥ kartavyaḥ tataḥ koṭhīmadhye babbūlakhadiram āmbalīprabhṛtīnāṃ līhālakaiḥ pūrayitvā yantraṃ ca tatra kṣiptvā punaḥ punar dhmātvā saṃdaṃśair adhomukhīṃ yantranalīṃ dhūtvā yāvanmātro raso madhyād galitvādhomūṣāyāṃ sameti tat khāparasattvaṃ kathyate || 3
body.translated_text: Then, sealing all sides without gaps using rag-and-clay, such an apparatus called <s>tumba-nālī</s> (gourd-tube) should be made for essence-extraction. Then, filling the interior of the furnace with charcoal of <s>babbūla</s> (acacia), <s>khadira</s> (catechu), <s>āmbalī</s> (tamarind), and similar [woods], placing the apparatus therein, blowing repeatedly, and shaking the downward-facing tube-apparatus with tongs — when the mercury melts from the middle and collects in the lower crucible, that is called the <s>khāpara sattva</s> (essence of zinc calx). ||3
Thus the method for extracting the essence of <s>khāpara</s> (zinc calx). ||4
Now, the method for extracting the essence of <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar):

children.translated_text: The finest <s>kaṇayarī</s> (granular variety) of <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar)
should be ground by the wise in a mortar;
having placed it in a glass pot,
the mouth should be covered with <s>abhraka</s> (ite).
One should place burned
stone-powder mixed with salt on the top;
the entire pot should be coated
with cloth and clay.
Having broken the neck of a fired pot
and placing the clay-coated pot [therein],
a strong fire should be kindled below
for twelve <s>yāmas</s> (watches, ~36 hours) per <s>maṇa</s>.
The interior of the pot becomes empty,
the essence descends to the neck;
having broken the pot, the <s>śilā sattva</s> (realgar essence)
should be carefully collected by the wise.

body.text: sarvottamā kaṇayarī manaḥśilā kharale piṣṭvā kumpe kṣiptvā abhrakeṇa kumpamukhaṃ pidhāya lavaṇasahitaṃ dagdhapāṣāṇacūrṇaṃ mastake dattvā vastramṛttikayā sarvāṃ kumpāṃ muktvādho manaḥśilāṃ prati praharadvādaśakaṃ yāvat haṭhāgnir jvālanīyaḥ || 1
body.translated_text: Having ground the finest <s>kaṇayarī</s> variety of <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) in a mortar and placed it in a pot, covering the pot's mouth with <s>abhraka</s> (mica), placing burned stone-powder mixed with salt on top, sealing the entire pot with cloth and clay — below, toward the <s>manaḥśilā</s>, a strong fire should be kindled for twelve <s>yāmas</s> (watches). ||1

body.text: tataḥ sattvamuḍḍīya kaṇṭhe lagati kumbhodaraṃ ca riktaṃ bhavati || 2
body.translated_text: Then the essence rises and adheres to the neck, and the interior of the pot becomes empty. ||2

body.text: evaṃ kumpaṃ bhaṅktvā kaṇṭhalagnaṃ sattvaṃ grāhyam || 3
body.translated_text: Thus, having broken the pot, the essence adhering to the neck should be collected. ||3
Thus the method for extracting the essence of <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar). ||4
Now, the three methods for making the liquefaction of the six metals, as follows: ||5

children.translated_text: A frog that has died naturally
is to be obtained from wherever available;
<s>sphaṭika</s> (crystal), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa kṣāra</s> (borax) —
their fine pieces [should be prepared].
Having split open the frog's belly,
those fine pieces should be placed inside;
the frog, smeared with ghee, oil, and the like,
should be placed in a pot.
Having placed a covering lid,
the pot is buried in the ground;
after sixty days have passed,
the pot should be pulled out from the earth.
From the middle of the pot, purely thus,
everything should be taken out;
having placed it all in a mortar,
it should be ground very finely.
Then, having melted one <s>gadyāṇa</s> (a small weight-unit)
of gold of fifteen <s>varṇa</s> (quality-grade),
into it, a <s>valla</s> (tiny quantity) of the frog-powder
should be added by the discerning.
The gold does not solidify;
it remains in liquid form —
this is the gold liquefaction produced,
accomplished indeed by the experts.
With a <s>valla</s> (tiny amount) placed within the gold,
just as the golden liquefaction results,
so too in <s>kāntaloha</s> (magnetic iron), in silver,
in <s>vaṅga</s> (tin), in <s>nāga</s> (lead), and likewise
in <s>tāmra</s> (copper) — in all six metals,
the powder penetrates sixteenfold;
and from among the six metals,
when any one is melted
in a <s>gadyāṇa</s> measure, a cloth-measure amount
of frog-powder should be added;
that metal becomes liquid in form —
the liquefaction is named after that [metal].
The sixfold metal liquefaction
is accomplished by experts through this procedure;
the operations that are performed with this
will be described in the [section on] minerals.

body.text: svabhāvena mṛtasya bhekasyodaraṃ vidārya sphāṭikojjvalaṭaṅkaṇakṣārasyātisūkṣmāḥ khoṭāṃs tatra kṣiptvā tato ghṛtatailādinā digdhvā madhye sthāli bhekaṃ muktvopari pradhvarāṃ ḍhaṅkaṇīyaṃ dattvā bhūmimadhye sthālī nikhanyate || 1
body.translated_text: Having split open the belly of a naturally dead frog, placing inside fine pieces of crystal-bright <s>ṭaṅkaṇa kṣāra</s> (borax), then smearing [the frog] with ghee, oil, and the like, placing the frog inside a pot, putting a covering lid on top, the pot is buried in the ground. ||1

body.text: ṣaṣṭidinaiḥ punaḥ sthālīmākṛṣya madhyātsarvaṃ gṛhītvā kharale piṣṭvā cūrṇaṃ kāryam || 2
body.translated_text: After sixty days, pulling the pot out again, taking everything from the middle, grinding it in a mortar, the powder should be made. ||2

body.text: tataḥ sarvottamaṃ suvarṇagadyāṇakaṃ gālayitvā vallamātraṃ bhekacūrṇaṃ madhye kṣipyate || 3
body.translated_text: Then, having melted one <s>gadyāṇa</s> of the finest gold, a <s>valla</s> (tiny amount) of the frog-powder is added into the middle. ||3

body.text: tatas tat suvarṇaṃ punarbandhaṃ nāpnoti kiṃtu dravameva tiṣṭhati || 4
body.translated_text: Then that gold no longer solidifies, but remains liquid. ||4
This is how the gold liquefaction is produced. ||5

body.text: iyaṃ ca suvarṇadrutirevaṃ kāntalohe rūpye vaṅge nāge tāmre ca gadyāṇamātre ca gālite vallamātraṃ bhekacūrṇaṃ kṣipyate || 6
body.translated_text: And this gold liquefaction [procedure works] similarly for <s>kāntaloha</s> (magnetic iron), silver, <s>vaṅga</s> (tin), <s>nāga</s> (lead), and <s>tāmra</s> (copper) — when a <s>gadyāṇa</s> measure of each is melted, a <s>valla</s> amount of frog-powder is added. ||6

body.text: tato dravarūpāṇi sarvāṇi bhaveyus tattannāmnī ca drutir bhavati || 7
body.translated_text: Then all become liquid in form, and the liquefaction is named after each respective [metal]. ||7
Iron-liquefaction, silver-liquefaction, tin-liquefaction, lead-liquefaction, and copper-liquefaction — thus. ||8
Thus the first [method of] making the six-metal liquefaction. ||9

children.translated_text: From the yellow <s>devadālī</s> (Luffa plant),
prepare the five parts and cut into pieces;
having burned them on a potsherd,
a fine ash should be made.
At the remaining end, of the five-parted
<s>niśāhvā</s> (turmeric), one should process [the ash];
with its own juice, the impregnation
of this very ash should be given.
When one <s>gadyāṇa</s> is melted
of fifteen-<s>varṇa</s> (quality) gold,
a <s>valla</s> of the ash should be added;
and then another <s>valla</s> should be added again.
Thus, into the <s>gadyāṇa</s>,
a [full] <s>gadyāṇa</s> [of ash] should always be digested;
in this way, the gold liquefaction is produced —
this procedure [applies to] all metals.

body.text: pañcāṅgapītadevadālīkhaṇḍāni kṛtvā karpare jvālayitvā gāḍhaṃ bhasma kriyate tatastasyā eva devadālyā rasena bhāvanā tasya bhasmano dātavyā || 1
body.translated_text: Having cut the five parts of the yellow <s>devadālī</s> (Luffa) plant into pieces and burning them on a potsherd, a strong ash is made. Then, impregnation of that ash with the juice of that very <s>devadālī</s> should be given. ||1

body.text: tataḥ pañcadaśavarṇikakāñcanagadyāṇakaṃ gālayitvā vallamātraṃ devadālībhasma kṣiptvā jāraṇīyam || 2
body.translated_text: Then, having melted one <s>gadyāṇa</s> of fifteen-<s>varṇa</s> gold, a <s>valla</s> amount of <s>devadālī</s> ash should be added and digested. ||2

body.text: evaṃ punaḥpunarvallamātrakṣepe yadā gadyāṇakamātraṃ bhasma jīrṇaṃ syāttadā kāñcanadrutir bhavati || 3
body.translated_text: Thus, when through repeated addition of <s>valla</s> amounts, a <s>gadyāṇa</s> measure of ash has been digested, then the gold liquefaction results. ||3
Similarly, by digesting <s>devadālī</s> ash into iron and other [metals] also, the liquefaction named after each respective [metal] results. ||4
Thus the second [method of] making the six-metal liquefaction. ||5

children.translated_text: One should burn on a potsherd the white
five parts of the <s>devadālī</s> (Luffa) plant;
twenty-one impregnations with cow's urine
should be given to the ash.
Then, in all six metals,
the previously stated procedure should be applied;
liquefaction results in the six metals
in this way — there is no doubt.

body.text: śvetadevadālipañcāṅgakhaṇḍāni kṛtvā karpare jvālayitvā bhasma kṛtvaikaviṃśatibhāvanāṃ gomūtreṇa bhasmano dattvā pūrvavat ṣaḍlohamadhye śvetadevadālībhasma lepyam || 1
body.translated_text: Having cut the five parts of the white <s>devadālī</s> into pieces, burning them on a potsherd, making ash, giving twenty-one impregnations of the ash with cow's urine — as before, the white <s>devadālī</s> ash should be applied into the six metals. ||1
The liquefaction of all metals results. ||2
Thus the third [method of] making the six-metal liquefaction. ||3
Thus the three varieties of the method for making metal liquefaction. ||4

children.translated_text: <s>Nāga</s> (lead) is killed by <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar);
<s>haritāla</s> (orpiment) [kills] <s>vaṅga</s> (tin);
<s>loha</s> (iron) by <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar);
<s>tāmra</s> (copper) by pure <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur).
Silver by <s>tila-mākṣika</s> (sesame-pyrite);
gold is killed by <s>nāga</s> (lead);
as the procedure was stated for <s>tāmra</s> (copper),
that same procedure [applies] in the five killings.

body.text: manaḥśilayā nāgaṃ haritālena vaṅgaṃ hiṅgulena lohaṃ śuddhagandhakena tāmraṃ tilamākṣikeṇa rūpyaṃ nāgena suvarṇaṃ ca mriyate || 1
body.translated_text: By realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>), lead is killed; by orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>), tin; by cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>), iron; by purified sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), copper; by sesame-pyrite (<s>tilamākṣika</s>), silver; and by lead (<s>nāga</s>), gold is killed. ||1
Then, 'by which method,' etc. ||2

children.translated_text: A leaf or powder of copper
should be separately prepared by the wise one.
Purified sulphur powder,
doubled in amount compared to the copper —
ground with the juice of <s>Kumārī</s> (aloe),
or with milk if that is unavailable.
Between two cakes of that [mixture],
one should place the copper leaf.
Inside a pair of shallow earthen dishes (<s>śarāvasampuṭa</s>),
having placed that and sealed with clay,
having sealed the joint with cloth and clay,
one should place the sealed [container] in a <s>kaṭāha</s> (large pan).
Having filled the <s>kaṭāha</s> with cow-dung cakes
and then kindled the fire,
when it has burned and cooled,
the copper should be taken out as 'killed' by the wise.

body.text: tāmrasya pattraṃ vā cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tatastāmraṃ dviguṇaṃ śuddhaṃ gandhakacūrṇaṃ kumārīrase nāgo dugdhena vā gāḍhaṃ mṛditvā pūpādvayaṃ ca kṛtvā madhye pūrvakṛtatāmrapattracūrṇaṃ vā kṣiptvā pūpādvayaṃ śarāvasampuṭe muktvā saṃdhau vastramṛttikayā liptvā sarvato mṛttikayā liptvā kaṭāhamadhye śarāvasampuṭe kṣiptvā chāṇakaiśca kaṭāhaṃ bhṛtvā nirjvālanīyaḥ || 1
body.translated_text: Having made a leaf or powder of copper, then: sulphur powder purified [and] doubled in amount compared to the copper, ground firmly with <s>Kumārī</s> juice (or milk from <s>nāga</s>), and having made two cakes, placing the previously prepared copper leaf or powder in the middle, putting the two cakes in a sealed pair of shallow dishes (<s>śarāvasampuṭa</s>), sealing the joint with cloth and clay, sealing all over with clay, placing the sealed container in the middle of a <s>kaṭāha</s>, filling the <s>kaṭāha</s> with cow-dung cakes, [the fire] should be burned out completely. ||1

body.text: tato jvalitvā śītale jāte sati tāmraṃ mṛtaṃ grāhyam || 2
body.translated_text: Then, when it has burned and cooled, the killed copper should be taken out. ||2
Thus the procedure for killing copper. ||3

body.text: yena vidhinā gandhakenātra tāmraṃ māritaṃ tenaiva vidhinā nāgādīni pañca lohāni kārye sati māraṇīyāni || 4
body.translated_text: By the very same method by which copper is killed here with sulphur, by that same method the five metals beginning with lead should be killed when needed. ||4
Thus the procedure for killing the six metals. ||5
Now, the threefold preparation of the food-path diamond (<s>annapathaḥ hīraka</s>), and the fivefold killing:

children.translated_text: The stalk of a <s>bījapūra</s> (citron) —
having pulled it out, one should make a cavity.
A genuine diamond (<s>hīraka</s>)
should be placed in the middle and covered with the stalk.
The entire <s>bījapūra</s>
should be wrapped with cloth and clay.
In length and depth and breadth,
a pit one cubit in measure [should be dug].
Having filled that pit with set cow-dung cakes,
the <s>bījapūra</s> [should be placed] in that pit;
covering the mouth with a potsherd,
one should then place fire in the middle.
When it has burned and cooled,
with fresh <s>bījapūras</s> each time,
again and again this procedure
should be performed nine times.
Rolling into very fine
cakes of <s>nisāhā</s> (<s>vaḍavāikā</s>),
one should place the diamond inside that ball;
the ball [should be placed] in a sealed pair of dishes.
The previously made pit should be filled
with set cow-dung cakes again.
Having sealed its back with cloth and clay,
the wise one should fire it inside the pit.
With fresh <s>vaḍavāikā</s> [cakes],
one should fire nine times repeatedly.
Then, a branch of the royal jujube (<s>rājabadarī</s>)
with tender shoots —
having taken that, the discerning one
should make a cavity inside it.
<s>Nesahiṅgu</s> (asafoetida paste) below and above
should be placed, and the diamond inserted.
With cloth and clay, [made] hole-free,
the branch with tender shoots —
in the previously made pit,
nine times, as before.
In a block of <s>nesahiṅgu</s>,
having made a cavity and [placed] the diamond,
covering the mouth with <s>hiṅgu</s>,
a <s>muṣa</s> (crucible) [is placed on] a <s>māṣapīṭhikā</s> (bean-paste platform).
Placing that in a vessel full of oil,
one should kindle fire below.
By this method, nine times it should be done,
in a fresh <s>hiṅgu</s>-block each time.
By this method, the three-path (<s>tripatha</s>) genuine
diamond clearly comes into being.
Having ground with <s>thūthā-viḍa</s> (copper-sulphate salt),
the wise one digests [it] in mercury.

body.text: bījapūrasya vṛntam utpāṭya madhye utkīrya randhraṃ kṛtvā tatra hīrakaṃ jātyaṃ kṣiptvopari vṛntenācchādya vastramṛttikayā samagraṃ bījapūrakaṃ veṣṭayitvā tato hastamātraṃ dīrghā hastamātraṃ pṛthulā hastamātraṃ cādha evaṃ gartāṃ kṛtvā sthāpitaiḥ chāṇakaiḥ pūrayitvā tatra bījapūrakaṃ muktvopari mukhe karparaṃ dattvā chāṇakeṣu vahnir deyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Having pulled out the stalk of a <s>bījapūra</s>, carved out the middle and made a cavity, placed a genuine diamond therein, covered it with the stalk above, and wrapped the entire <s>bījapūra</s> with cloth and clay — then having dug a pit one cubit in length, one cubit in width, and one cubit in depth, filling it with set cow-dung cakes, placing the <s>bījapūra</s> therein, covering the mouth with a potsherd, fire should be applied to the cow-dung cakes.

body.text: tato jvalitvā śītalībhūte vīḍāpūrvaṃ tataḥ punardvitīyaṃ bījapūramānīya pūrvavatsarvaṃ kṛtvā gartāyāṃ hīrakabījapūre kṣiptvā chāṇakāni jvālayitvā śītalībhūte sati bījapūramadhyāddhīrako grāhyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then, when it has burned and cooled, having taken out the <s>vīḍā</s> (betel preparation) first, then bringing a second <s>bījapūra</s>, performing everything as before, placing the diamond-<s>bījapūra</s> in the pit, kindling the cow-dung cakes, and when cooled, the diamond should be taken from the middle of the <s>bījapūra</s>.

body.text: evaṃ navanavavāraṃ navanavair bījapūraiḥ sa eva hīrakaḥ pacanīyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus nine times with nine fresh <s>bījapūras</s>, that same diamond should be fired.

body.text: tato vaḍavāikānisāhāyāṃ vartayitvā tat piṇḍaṃ kṛtvā tatra madhye sa eva hīrakaḥ kṣepyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then, having rolled the <s>vaḍavāikā</s>-<s>nisāhā</s> [into a paste], making that into a ball, that same diamond should be placed in the middle.

body.text: tatastaṃ piṇḍaṃ śarāvasampuṭāntaḥ kṣiptvā sarvato vastramṛttikayā liptvā pūrvataḥ kṛtagartāṃ chāṇakaiḥ bhṛtvā tasyāṃ gartāyāṃ śarāvasampuṭaṃ madhye muktvāgnir jvālanīyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then, placing that ball inside a sealed pair of dishes, sealing all over with cloth and clay, filling the previously made pit with cow-dung cakes, placing the sealed pair of dishes in the middle of the pit, fire should be kindled.

children.text: * tataḥ śītalībhūte punaranyāsāṃ vaḍavāikānāṃ piṇḍamadhye tameva hīrakaṃ kṣiptvā tathaiva jvālayitvā hīrako grāhyaḥ |
children.translated_text: * Then, when cooled, again placing that same diamond in the middle of a ball of other <s>vaḍavāikā</s> [cakes], kindling likewise, the diamond should be taken out.

children.text: * evaṃ navavāraṃ navanavābhir vaḍavāikābhiḥ sa eva pacanīyaḥ rājabadaryāḥ kisalayarūpāṃ komalāṃ śākhāmānīya tasyāṃ chidraṃ kṛtvā nesahiṅguṃ tatrādha ūrdhvaṃ ca dattvā chidramadhye tameva hīrakaṃ kṣiptvā vastramṛttikayā nicchādya pūrvaṃ chāṇakapūrṇagartāyāṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: * Thus nine times with nine fresh <s>vaḍavāikā</s> [cakes], that same [diamond] should be fired. Having brought a tender branch of the royal jujube, making a hole in it, placing <s>nesahiṅgu</s> below and above, inserting that same diamond in the middle of the hole, sealing all with cloth and clay, it should be fired in the pit previously filled with cow-dung cakes.

body.text: tataḥ punarbadarīśākhākisalayacchidre hīrakaṃ kṣiptvā tathaiva gartāyāṃ pacanīyaḥ || 2
body.translated_text: Then, again inserting the diamond in a hole in a jujube branch shoot, it should be fired likewise in the pit. ||2

body.text: evaṃ navavāraṃ navanavo rājabadarīśākhākisalayaiḥ sa eva hīrakaḥ pacanīyaḥ || 3
body.translated_text: Thus nine times with nine fresh royal jujube branch shoots, that same diamond should be fired. ||3

body.text: tato mahato nesahiṅgukhoṭasya madhye randhraṃ kṛtvā tameva hīrakaṃ kṣiptvā mukhaṃ ca nesahiṅgunā ācchādyopari māṣapīṭhīṃ dadyāt tatastailapūrṇe pātre taṃ hiṅgukhoṭaṃ kṣiptvādho 'gnir jvālanīyaḥ || 4
body.translated_text: Then, having made a cavity in the middle of a large <s>nesahiṅgu</s> block, placing that same diamond, covering the mouth with <s>nesahiṅgu</s>, placing a bean-paste [platform] on top — then, placing that <s>hiṅgu</s> block in an oil-filled vessel, fire should be kindled below. ||4
Then, again in a fresh <s>hiṅgu</s> block, likewise. ||5

body.text: evaṃ navavāraṃ navanavair nesahiṅgukhoṭaiḥ sa eva hīrakaḥ pacanīyaḥ || 6
body.translated_text: Thus nine times with nine fresh <s>nesahiṅgu</s> blocks, that same diamond should be fired. ||6

children.text: * thūthāviḍena taṃ hīrakaṃ sampiṣya pūrvokte rase śanaiḥ śanairjāraṇīyo hīrakaḥ |
children.translated_text: * Having ground that diamond with <s>thūthā-viḍa</s> (copper-sulphate salt), the diamond should be slowly digested in the previously mentioned mercury.
* Thus the first [method of] digestion of the food-path diamond.
From the ears of she-buffaloes,
ear-wax should be collected in its entirety.
With that, the wise one should wrap
genuine diamonds, [the substance] that bestows wealth.
Having placed that in <s>Sūraṇa</s> (elephant-yam) small tubers,
and wrapping with cloth and clay,
a 'rooster'-type crucible firing (<s>kurkuṭapuṭa</s>)
should be given [in a pit] in the ground.
Again and again, with [fresh] ear-wax
and <s>Sūraṇa</s> small tubers,
with fresh cloth and clay,
the crucible firings should be given.
With twenty-one repetitions
of rooster-type firings in the ground,
the diamonds are easily made
into the 'food-path' form by the wise.

body.text: mahiṣīṇāṃ karṇamalān gṛhītvā jātyān hīrān veṣṭayitvā tair malaistato malaveṣṭitāṃstān sūraṇakṣudrakandeṣu chidrāṇi kṛtvā tatra ca kṣiptvā sarvataḥ karpaṭamṛttikayā liptvā bhūmau kurkuṭapuṭo dātavyaḥ || 1
body.translated_text: Having taken the ear-wax of she-buffaloes, wrapping genuine diamonds with it, then — having made holes in <s>Sūraṇa</s> small tubers and placing the wax-wrapped [diamonds] therein, sealing all over with cloth and clay — a rooster-type crucible firing should be given in the ground. ||1

body.text: tataḥ punar hīrakaṃ gṛhītvā tathaiva mahiṣīkarṇamalair veṣṭayitvā sūraṇakṣudrakandamadhye kṣiptvā vastramṛttikayā sarvato liptvā bhūmau chāṇakaiḥ kurkuṭapuṭo deyaḥ || 2
body.translated_text: Then, again taking out the diamond, wrapping likewise with buffalo ear-wax, placing in the middle of a <s>Sūraṇa</s> small tuber, sealing all over with cloth and clay, a rooster-type crucible firing should be given in the ground with cow-dung cakes. ||2

body.text: evaṃ punaḥ punarekaviṃśativārān mahiṣīkarṇamalena veṣṭayitvā sūraṇakṣudrakaṃ teṣu ca kṣiptvā bhūmau kurkuṭapuṭān dattvānnapathyahīrakāḥ sādhanīyāḥ || 3
body.translated_text: Thus, again and again twenty-one times, wrapping with buffalo ear-wax, [placing in] <s>Sūraṇa</s> small tubers, and giving rooster-type crucible firings in the ground — the food-path diamonds should be prepared. ||3
Thus the second method of making diamonds into the food-path form. ||4

children.translated_text: Of the earth-plant <s>Mardakī</s>,
the tender leaves should be rolled.
Inside that ball, having placed
the diamonds, make a sphere.
Placing that in a sealed pair of dishes
and wrapping the joint with cloth and clay,
a crucible firing should be given
of the rooster type in the ground.
With all fresh [materials] each time,
sixty-four rooster-type
crucible firings should be given —
[then] the diamonds are made into the food-path form.

body.text: yā bhūmyā mardakī bhūmiphoḍī tasyāḥ pattrāṇi komalāni vartayitvā piṇḍīṃ ca kṛtvā madhye jātyahīrakān kṣiptvā golakān kṛtvā tān śarāvasampuṭamadhye muktvā saṃdhau karpaṭamṛttikāṃ ca dattvā bhūmau kurkuṭapuṭaṃ dātavyam || 1
body.translated_text: The earth-plant <s>Mardakī</s> is <s>Bhūmiphoḍī</s>. Having rolled its tender leaves and made a ball, placing genuine diamonds in the middle, making spheres, placing those in the middle of a sealed pair of dishes, putting cloth and clay at the joint — a rooster-type crucible firing should be given in the ground. ||1

body.text: tataḥ punastathaiva bhūmyāmardakīpiṇḍīmadhye hīrān kṣiptvā golakān kṛtvā śarāvasampuṭe ca kṣiptvā karpaṭamṛttikāṃ ca saṃdhau dattvā bhūmau kurkuṭapuṭo deyaḥ || 2
body.translated_text: Then, again placing diamonds in the middle of a <s>Bhūmyāmardakī</s> leaf ball, making spheres, placing in a sealed pair of dishes, putting cloth and clay at the joint — a rooster-type crucible firing should be given in the ground. ||2

body.text: evaṃ navanavair bhūmyāmardakīpattrapiṇḍīgolakaiste hīrakā bhūmau catuḥṣaṣṭiṃ kurkuṭapuṭāni dattvānnapathāḥ kāryāḥ || 3
body.translated_text: Thus, with nine-times-fresh <s>Bhūmyāmardakī</s> leaf-ball spheres, the diamonds should be given sixty-four rooster-type crucible firings in the ground and made into the food-path form. ||3
This is the meaning: ||4
They become cooked like food, and are digested in the mercury. ||5
Thus the third method of making diamonds into the food-path form. ||6

children.translated_text: It is not burned by fire,
it is not broken when struck with hammers,
it does not sink in water —
it is indeed difficult to test.
Having placed lac (<s>līlaka</s>) in the palms
and twenty diamonds,
they should be rubbed with the hands —
those that do not lose their luster [are genuine].
Those in which not a single scratch appears —
those are known as genuine diamonds.
Having brought a fired potsherd,
many cavities should be made.
Genuine diamonds should be placed in those,
and then with [bellows worked by] the dead and living,
blowing and blowing, the potsherd should be made
fire-colored by the experts.
Human urine and <s>thauhara</s> (calx) milk,
mixed equally together —
with that, the blown potsherd
should be quenched again and again.
In fresh potsherds,
having made cavities and [placed] the diamonds,
those same [diamonds] should be placed and blown;
the blown ones should be quenched with the mixture.
By this method, blowing seven times
